"Due to the authority of the transformation from Blooming to Radiant," she explained, her voice echoing with pride, "I was able to accelerate the process of the budding of new Inevitabilities.
Those nine there... they should be ready soon."
As if her words were a cue for reality itself, prompts began to rise before Noah's eyes, their text glowing with the same obsidian-crimson light as the cocoons.
|The Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary has been successfully forged as a new feature of the Radiant Shore.|
|Primary Function: From the conceptual soil of this sanctuary, the Seeds of Inevitability will naturally sprout and bloom.|
|Spawning Cycle: Every 24 hours, an unknown number of Inevitability Cocoons will manifest.|
|Nutrient Dependency: The quantity and quality of the Inevitabilities produced is directly proportional to the nutrients fed into the Ranch.
Higher quality nutrients will yield more powerful and numerous progeny.|
|Current Status: Under the Blessing of The First Hunger, the growth of Inevitabilities is accelerated exponentially.
All Inevitabilities born while this blessing is active will possess a minimum of 50 Trillion in Complexity or Purity.|
|Ranch Features Unlocked:|
|- The Nursery: Where new cocoons form and mature.|
|- Feeding Trough: A designated area where nutrients (Corpses, Ores, Treasures, Everythings) can be deposited to fuel the Ranch.|
|- Happiness Meter: Each Inevitability possesses a 'Mood.' Happier Inevitabilities mature faster and have a chance to develop unique, beneficial traits.
Mood can be improved through proper feeding and... petting.|
|- Specialized Diet: Feeding the Ranch specific types of Everythings (e.g., Everything of Destruction, Everything of Growth) will influence the type of Inevitabilities that are born.|
Noah's analysis of the prompts was a silent, incandescent flash of wonder.
He looked at Khor, and his appreciation for this ancient, terrifying being deepened.
He was seeing a glimpse of her true power, not as a warrior, but as a cultivator of the very forces that others saw only as mindless destruction.
He was reminded of what he had seen of her in the Earliest Folds, in that nest of obsidian and hunger.
This was her home element!
Khor turned to him, her ancient, abyssal eyes sparkling with a vibrant, youthful light.
"So, Outsider, it's a glorious thing, isn't it?" she asked, her voice filled with genuine warmth.
"I've missed seeing the young'uns, and many come out looking so cute..."
Her terrifying words were punctuated by a new set of prompts, blooming like dark flowers in his vision.
|Due to the boon of The First Hunger, the first round of Inevitabilities has been brought to maturity.|
|They are breaking out of their Nests.|
WU!
WU!
WU!
The nine obsidian-crimson cocoons began to pulse violently.
Cracks, like veins of molten lava, spread across their crystalline surfaces.
Then, with a sound that was less a crack and more a tearing of reality, terrifying black tentacles shot out from the fissures, whipping through the air with a hungry hiss.
The very atmosphere grew thick with the raw, untamed aura of appetite.
The shells shattered, exploding outward in a shower of obsidian shards.
From the wreckage, nine wriggling, circular masses of pure Inevitability spilled forth.
They were glorious, horrifying things, each a vortex of countless, intertwined tentacles, their forms constantly shifting, their very existence a defiance of stable geometry.
And yet, from the center of each roiling mass, pairs of innocent, stellar obsidian eyes blinked open.
They gazed out at the new world, at the Radiant Shore, at Noah and Khor, with a pure, unadulterated curiosity.
They looked at Khor with a fondness that transcended instinct; it was a deep, primal recognition.
Eight of the massive, writhing beings floated towards her, nudging her tiny figure lovingly with bodies that could have crushed Dukes.
She laughed, a sound of pure delight, as she stroked their tentacled forms, cooing at them in a language that predated words.
One, however, went towards Noah.
It was a perfect sphere of writhing, obsidian tentacles, its stellar eyes wide and inquisitive.
It sniffed at him, its senses not of smell but of conceptual resonance.
Then, its pupils, which were miniature galaxies of want, curved into crescent smiles.
The massive body of the Inevitability brushed against Noah's chest with a gesture of pure, uncomplicated affection.
Noah stood in the midst of this impossible scene, a faint smile on his lips.
He reached out and patted the massive, writhing creature, feeling the shocking, immense power that pulsed just beneath its surface.
|Nine new Inevitabilities have been born in the Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary.|
|Each possesses a base Complexity or Purity exceeding 50 Trillion.|
|Rearing Note: The growth and maturation of Inevitabilities is intrinsically linked to the health and power of the Early Veiled Shore.|
|Dietary Requirement: To mature further and unlock their full potential, Inevitabilities are most fond of a single food source: Everythings.|
|Task Assignment: Mature Inevitabilities can be assigned tasks, such as guarding the Shore or... hunting.|
Noah observed the prompts, his eyes shining with a universe of possibilities.
He looked at the creature still rubbing affectionately against his chest, and his mind, now free of fear and doubt, saw not a pet, but a weapon.
A tool.
A new, terrifyingly efficient method of harvest!
He could now deploy these beings, these pure expressions of hunger, to devour the Everythings of his enemies and nurture them into terrifying, loyal weapons!
As he thought this, his eyes flashed with a bloody purple light.
Before him, the status sheet of the newly born Inevitability rose, clear and stark against the radiant backdrop of the Shore.
|Nascent Inevitability of Voracious Joy|
|Complexity: 0|
|Distinctions:|
|- The Newborn: Possesses immense potential for growth and is highly impressionable.
Its final nature will be determined by the Everythings it consumes and the guidance of its master.|
|- Voracious Joy: A unique trait.
This Inevitability finds genuine, childlike happiness in the act of consumption.
This makes it particularly effective at devouring positive concepts like Hope, Courage, and Love.|
|- Primordial Bond: Irreversibly bound to The Early Creature, Osmont.
Its loyalty is absolute, its hunger an extension of its master's will.|
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4197 Powerful! I
paragraphs: The moment was surreal.
Days ago, a measure of time that felt both impossibly long and laughably short...the very concept of an Inevitability had been a distant, terrifying abstraction.
They were the stuff of legends, the mindless hunger that pruned the branches of existence!

If someone had told him then that he would one day stand on a shore of his own making, with a newborn, fifty-trillion-purity Inevitability nudging affectionately against his chest like a housecat seeking attention, he would have deemed them fucking insane.
Those Inevitabilities? The ones that devoured everything? Hah!
Yet, here he was.

He ran a hand over the writhing, paradoxical surface of the creature before him. The tentacles were not solid, not liquid, but something in between, a texture like solidified impossibility that was both smooth and infinitely complex.
They pulsed with a gentle warmth, a nascent, innocent hunger that had not yet learned the cruelty of the wider Folds.
He was in complete control. He felt the unbreakable bond thrumming between his existence and that of the nine new beings born from his Shore.
They were extensions of his will, weapons forged in a crucible of his own design.
Khor floated beside him, her ancient, abyssal eyes regarding the scene with a thoughtful smile.

"A measure of a good existence," she said, her voice a soft, melodic hum against the quiet backdrop of the Radiant Shore, "is whether a Young Inevitability likes them or not. You may just be a good existence, Outsider."

Noah blinked at her words, a faint, almost imperceptible smile touching his lips. "Well," he replied, his tone calm and measured as he continued to pat the tentacles of the adoring creature, "this good man is planning to have these Inevitabilities consume the Everythings of Dead Existences. There are nine of them right now, but there will be more and more in the future. You wouldn't have any issues with me commanding them and sending them out of the Shore?"
He was probing, testing the boundaries of her philosophy, of his control.

He held her Symbolic Heart of Hunger, a supposed guarantee of absolute authority. But the more he witnessed her power, the more he suspected that for a being like Khor, absolutes were merely suggestions.
She might just be capable of breaking free of his control whenever she truly wished.

Khor's smile widened, her eyes sparkling with a mischievous light. "Outsider, the Way of Existence of Inevitabilities is to devour. I would encourage you to send them out so that they could live freely. If any perish in their journey... then it was simply meant to be. That is their way."
She paused, her gaze turning thoughtful as she surveyed the sprawling, magnificent Shore.

"But is it not interesting? THE Loom is supposedly surrounded by countless Inevitabilities, and now you have Inevitabilities in your Shore. Even though there are only nine currently, when you have thousands, or millions... you actually begin imitating THE Loom."

She laughed, a sound like stars colliding in a distant galaxy. "Haha, maybe your solution of turning your Shore into a bastion that could withstand whatever is coming is more viable than you believe."
HUUM!
Noah's eyes shone with a sharp, tyrannical light. The idea resonated with a deep, fundamental part of his being.
Not just to survive, but to build his own sanctuary, his own version of THE Loom!
"Let's hope that's the case," he said, his voice a low murmur. "I'll continue seeking this solution. And also all the other ones..."
He turned his attention back to the nine creatures before him, his demeanor shifting from contemplative to commanding.
He did not need to raise his voice; his will alone was a shout that echoed through their nascent consciousnesses.
"Attention!"
As if he were a drill sergeant and his words were law, the nine writhing masses of hunger, each exceeding fifty trillion in either complexity or purity, snapped into a perfectly straight line.
Their stellar obsidian eyes, once filled with innocent happiness, now held a focused, eager attention.
Noah looked at them, a general surveying his new, impossible army. "Do you want to devour Everythings?"
The response was a glorious, silent explosion of enthusiasm. Their tentacles waved wildly, a forest of writhing, eager appendages.
A collective, psychic YES! boomed through the Shore.

He nodded, a gesture of profound satisfaction. With a wave of his hand, thousands of sparkling, milky-white drops of the Sacred Mead of Existence materialized in the air, a celestial rain of pure, concentrated potential.
The taste and elevation it offered were unrivaled, and the tentacles of the Young Inevitabilities shot out with lightning speed, snatching the falling drops with gleeful hunger.
Noah's eyes softened as he watched them feast. "Enjoy this," he said, his voice a gentle murmur that carried across the sands. "Soon, you will be deployed to fight The Dead."
WUU! WUU!
A chorus of cute, eager sounds of agreement erupted from the nine creatures, as if the prospect of facing the ultimate anathema to life was the most exciting thing they had ever heard.
He shook his head, a smile touching his lips. He turned back to Khor, who had been watching the scene with a fond, almost maternal expression.
"Are there any other wonders that you messed with? When it comes to the Early Veiled Shore and what it can now do as a Radiant Shore."
Khor blinked and looked away, a flicker of something that looked suspiciously like guilt crossing her ancient features.
She coughed, a delicate, soundless gesture. "Well, I didn't really do too much," she said, her tone a little too nonchalant. "But I did tweak a little something regarding your Sacred Totems."
His Sacred Totems.
Noah's attention sharpened. It was long overdue for him to ring another, to call forth a new Land Lifeform.
Heidrun, his first, was providing indispensable resources, her Mead of Existence a cornerstone of his rapid advancement.

Yoshinami, his second, was a weapon of absolute, terrifying power, capable of decimating anything below a Quadrillion in complexity. He knew he needed to elevate them both further; the corpses of The Dead would serve as perfect nutrients.
If he could get Yoshinami to the point where she could act multiple times a day, and against foes of ten or fifty quadrillion... the possibilities were heavy!
He turned his gaze to the distant pastures, where a certain majestic white goat was arrogantly nibbling on verdant-gold herbs.
His stare must have carried some weight, for Heidrun shivered, her head snapping up to look at him with a suspicious, almost accusatory glare!

chapters.title: Chapter 4198 Powerful! II
paragraphs: Noah smiled, his attention returning to Khor.
"What changes have been made to the capabilities of the Sacred Totems?"
Khor's smile turned brilliant, all pretense of guilt vanishing.

"Beforehand, you could call out to Land Lifeforms...unique creatures with an intricate connection to an Early Veiled Shore, a tradition dating back to their first design by THE Creature and THE Living Existences. But now," she giggled, a sound that made the air itself seem to bubble with mischief, "in addition to Land Lifeforms... huhu, you may be able to call something out from even the Earliest Folds and force it to be bound as an Early Living Land Lifeform!"
BOOM!

The words were a thunderclap in the quiet of Noah's mind. To summon a being from that primordial era, a place where the rules of existence were still being written, and bind it to his service... it was a power that defied many other powers!

His gaze swept across the Radiant Shore, at the dozens of Sacred Totems that rose like lighthouses of white-gold and obsidian, their light reaching into dimensions he was only just beginning to comprehend.

He closed his eyes, sensing his Early Atlas of the Folds. The weavings of Cheats were still at work, its golden light moving across his internal star chart, relentlessly pushing more of his Towers of Osmont toward the Third Stage.
As of this moment, all one hundred and fifty-nine of them had achieved the Second Stage.
When he rang one, the others would resonate. What impossible creature would answer such a call? He didn't need to guess!
He began to walk, his steps sure and steady, toward a tower that pulsed with a particular, arrogant brilliance.
The Sacred Totem of Cheats. Since that authority had been working so tirelessly on his behalf, he wanted to see what ringing its bell would achieve!
Khor floated along beside him.

He glanced at her, at this being of impossible power who had so freely given him these world-altering upgrades. "You continue to help me freely, even without being asked. How do you want to be repaid?"
At his words, Khor frowned, a look of genuine offense on her ancient, youthful face.

"Outsider, when your Moiraine or your Infiniverse or your Ruination help you, do you consider how to repay them? No. You consider them part of your forces... even as your family. There is no obligation of reciprocation there, is there?"

She paused, her expression softening. "Besides, you already planted my seed and allowed me to come back from collapse. If we start thinking in this manner, maybe it is me who still needs to repay you greatly. We can begin to think like that. Or..." She hummed, a thoughtful, melodic note. "We can simply... be, Outsider. After all, you and I are tied together now, are we not?"
Noah couldn't help but smile.
He reached the bottom of the massive, white-gold tower, its surface shimmering with a light that seemed to bend the rules of physics.
He looked at Khor, at her mischievous eyes.
"Tied together with The First Hunger. Okay," he said, his voice a low, resonant promise. "Let's accomplish some ridiculous things."
WAA!
He began to climb. The steps of the tower spiraled upward, each one a testament to the concept of bypassing limitations.
As he ascended, his mind was a whirlwind of thought.

In the Transcenent Origin Folds, the endless tide of The Dead was sweeping in. The Veil was thinning. The signs were all there, pointing toward the coming Fallout, the event that even THE Living Paradox sought to escape.
He felt as if he were in a race against time itself, a race where the finish line was unknown and the stakes were absolute.
But depending on how much time he had, he had the utmost confidence in his survival, and the survival of all those under him.
The only problem was, this time around, he truly did not know how much time there was.
So he could only move forward. He could only be desperate!
He reached the top of the tower, the air here humming with the raw, untamed authority of Cheats.

He stood before the massive, crystalline bell, ready to toll it, ready to call forth something grand. His body became wreathed in the bloody purple flames of his Haki, his Heart pulsing with a powerful, tyrannical rhythm!
He would call out, and something from the deepest, most impossible corners of existence would answer!
At the apex of the Tower of Cheats, reality itself seemed to hold its breath.
The structure was a monument of white-gold, a defiant statement against the very concept of limitation, and at its summit, a brilliant bell of the same material hung in perfect, silent stillness.

Beside it, a golden rope, woven from threads of pure possibility, dangled from an anchor point that existed in more dimensions than were strictly necessary. It waited not to be pulled, but to be commanded!

Noah stood before it, his form a tempest of contained power. The bloody purple flames of his Haki coiled around his muscles, a royal conflagration that danced with the rhythm of his impossibly powerful Heart.

He was a being forged in the crucible of desperation, and in his eyes, there was a cold, tyrannical fire that had burned away all traces of the man he once was. He looked at the rope, at the bell, and he knew what needed to be done.
He reached out, his hand grasping the golden rope. The moment his fingers made contact, a shockwave of his will erupted across the Radiant Shore!

On all 159 other Sacred Totems, from the Tower of Quintessence to the Tower of Tyranny, illusory hands of bloody purple flame materialized, each one taking hold of a golden rope. He was not just ringing a bell; he was conducting a symphony!
If it had been before...before he had poured his very essence, his Complexity, his Purity, his Everything of Size into his heart- this act would have been an arduous, draining struggle. But now?
"Toll for me," he spoke, his voice not a request, but a tyrannical command!
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4199 Powerful! III
paragraphs: He pulled!
And across the vast, impossible expanse of the Shore, one hundred and fifty-nine bells began to ring as one.
|You are exerting tremendous effort to toll the bells of your Radiant Shore. This is a declaration of your will upon existence.|
|All this effort will undoubtedly lead to a tremendous harvest.|
|The Principle of Perpetual Harvest is putting its full, undivided weight behind this ordeal.|
The sound was a glorious, world-shaking thing!
It was not a cacophony, but a perfect, impossible harmony.

Each bell sang with its own unique note...the crisp, clear tone of Cheats, the deep, resonant hum of Tyranny, the bright, unwavering chime of Quintessence...yet they all wove together into a single, unified hymn.
It was a sound that did not travel through the air, but through the very soul of the Shore, a melody of power and glory that resonated in the bones of every being present!
|The Sacred Bells of multiple Sacred Totems have been rung simultaneously with a level of majesty unlike ever before.|
|All beings who hear the unified tolling, regardless of their power or complexity, will earn the right and the methodology to form Kleos Glyphs of their own Authorities.|
Across the golden sands, heads turned. Amelia Osmont, her form still glowing with the aftermath of her own impossible elevation, looked up with pride.
The Emperor Penguin, mid-waddle, froze and struck a pose of profound enlightenment. This faker!
Many paused!
Even the newly hatched Inevitabilities paused their playful consumption of Mead, their innocent, stellar eyes turning toward the source of the magnificent sound.
At the base of the Tower of Cheats, Khor floated, her usual mischievous smile replaced by a look of deep, ancient solemnity.
She could feel something else in the tolling of these bells, something vast and heavy being pulled from the spaces between existence.
Her abyssal eyes turned toward the distant, roiling mists at the edge of the Shore, her gaze sharp and concentrated. Something was coming!
|The tolling of the bells has been deemed... Tyrannically Quintessential!|
As the hymns reached a glorious, soul-shaking crescendo, the gray mists in the distance began to churn with a violent, purposeful energy.
They roiled and split, and from the newly formed chasm, a sliver of pure, absolute obsidian light began to bleed through.

Noah stopped ringing, his hands releasing the ropes. The echoes of the bells continued to ring, a lingering symphony of power, as he stood at the edge of the tower, his gaze fixed on the approaching anomaly.
|The calls of multiple Sacred Totems have been answered by a Transcendent Kleos Early Living Land Lifeform.|
He frowned. From that blazing obsidian light, he sensed not power or glory, but a maelstrom of raw, undiluted emotion!
Immense hatred, a rage that could burn Folds, and a profound sense of taboo, of something that should have remained hidden, forgotten.
And yet, as the light coalesced, it formed the image not of a monster, but of a man. A regal, impossibly noble-looking man!
|Pulled from the weavings of Collapse from the Earliest Folds, directed by the immense weight of Cheats and all other Sacred Totems... the Transcendent Kleos Lifeform, Malphas, has arrived.|
HUUM!
His entrance was a masterpiece of silent, terrible grandeur. He was adorned in what looked like ancient, obsidian royal clothing, the fabric seeming to drink the very light from the Shore.
His visage was tall and grand, his hair as dark as a starless night, and his eyes... his eyes shone with a terrifying crimson light.
He was beautiful, in the way a perfectly forged executioner's blade is beautiful, his figure muscular and toned, his face that of a man in his absolute prime!
He appeared, and for a moment, he simply stood there, his eyes closed as if breathing in the air of this new reality.
Then he opened them. That terrifying crimson glint, a light of pure, intelligent malice, turned and fixed upon Noah from across the vast distance of the Shore!
He took a single step.
And he arrived, not at the edge of the Shore, but at the very base of the Sacred Totem, where he immediately, without hesitation, knelt.
Noah looked down at this impossible being, then jumped from the top of the tower, landing silently before him.
The overwhelming torrent of hatred and rage he had sensed before had vanished.
Now, he sensed nothing from this grand, kneeling entity but a perfect, unnerving calm.
In his kneeling position, Malphas raised his head, his crimson eyes meeting Noah's.
His voice, when he spoke, was a smooth, cultured baritone, each word a perfectly polished gem of deference and respect.
"It is an immeasurable honor to be bound under the light of the True Emperor of Tyranny. I, Malphas, greet The Master."
His entire bearing was a paradox. He looked like a handsome devil, radiated the memory of unimaginable fury, yet acted as the most perfect, humble servant!
Noah's eyes flashed, a silent acknowledgment of the title.
"Malphas... show me who you are."
With a grace that was almost hypnotic, Malphas rose from his kneeling position and performed a deep, formal bow.
He raised his hand as if holding something, and from his palm, shockingly, a status sheet materialized, a scroll of pure, informational light that he presented to Noah.
|Malphas - The Cruel Attendant, The Crow|
|Distinction: Transcendent Kleos Early Living Land Lifeform|
|State: Fractured Existence (Current form represents a fraction of original power)|
|Complexity: 1,000,000,000,000,000 (1 Quadrillion)|

|Primary Ability - Panoptic Gaze: Can exert his perception to observe any location across the Folds. The clarity and duration of observation are dependent on the complexity of the target location. Can currently observe entire Folds with perfect clarity.|

|Primordial Bond: Irreversibly bound to The Early Creature, Osmont. Its loyalty is absolute, and all it does is an extension of its master's will. For the sake of his master, any methods will be employed. Any. Methods. But he does have a tendency towards cruelty.|
|Contained Everythings: This being is a vessel for an overabundance of the Everythings of Loyalty, Hatred, Rage, Fear, Insecurity, and Sorrow, all willingly given to him by his old Master.|
|Distinction - The Unflinching Witness: Can observe and record events of catastrophic magnitude without suffering existential or psychological damage.|
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4200 Powerful! IV
paragraphs: Noah's reaction was a solemn, heavy silence.
The numbers were terrifying, but it was the other details that truly resonated.
A Fractured Existence, holding this much power with only a fraction of his being!
The ability to observe entire Folds. And the Everythings... a being literally filled to the brim with the concentrated negative emotions of another.
Khor floated beside him, her brow furrowed in a rare expression of genuine surprise. "This... is unexpected."

The moment her voice echoed out, Malphas turned and bowed toward her. "I have only heard glimpses of your grace and power, but it is an honor to see The First Hunger, and to even be bound to the same Master."
After these words, Noah's mind, still processing the terrifying status sheet, focused on the most critical question. "Who was your previous Master?"

Malphas remained calm, his crimson eyes holding a deep, ancient sadness. "My previous Master, from the little that I can remember, felt an overwhelming sense of emotions. They gave me their Everythings of Hatred, Rage, Fear, Insecurity... alongside the Everything of Loyalty. They were unique, in that their Everythings regenerated, especially their negative emotions. I received these Everythings again and again."
Malphas gave a light bow and closed his eyes.
"My previous Master was THE Living Emotive, Master."
BOOM!
The name was a thunderclap in the quiet of the Shore. Even Khor was surprised!
The servant of one of the most mysterious and dangerous of THE Living Existences, a being whose actions had seeded existence with perpetual suffering, was now bound to him.

Malphas continued, his voice unwavering. "But our relationship ended when my Existence was collapsed. I do not know how I am standing before you today but... I only stand before you as your humble servant. All I wish... is to not be discarded as I was before. To not be collapsed. And I will do everything in my power to serve."
His eyes flashed with a regal, crimson brilliance as he bowed again toward Noah.
This was a terrifying being, a tool of unimaginable potential. Even in his fractured state, his power was on the level of the weakest Early Creatures! What had he been at his peak?
Noah looked at this entity, this noble butler who was a vessel of ancient pain and absolute loyalty, and he replied.
"From this day on, you are my servant, and the servant of the Early Veiled Shore."
A devilish, handsome smile bloomed on Malphas's face!
It was an expression of pure, unadulterated joy. His crimson eyes flashed with a terrifying intellect!
"For me to be able to use my capability to help Master to the utmost, is it okay if I tap into more of Master's current records of what is happening, what has happened, and is bound to happen?"
He asked for permission. Noah gave a light nod.
Malphas closed his eyes for but a second before they snapped open, now burning with a terrible, crimson light.
He had learned everything!
The state of the Folds, the threat of The Dead, the coming Fallout, Noah's impossible journey. His expression turned solemn. He looked at Noah, his gaze now filled with a profound understanding.

"I understand now how I can best be of service to My Lord," he said, his voice a low, determined vow. "I will do everything I can to ensure that you, and all those under you... do not experience collapse as I once did."
He would make sure that what happened to him, that utter, soul-crushing collapse, did not happen to Noah!
The vow was a silent, unshakeable thing in the core of Malphas's fractured existence. It was the one piece of his shattered self that felt whole, the one purpose that had survived the unmaking.
He stood before his new Lord, a regal, obsidian figure against the radiant white-gold backdrop of the Shore, his bearing a perfect paradox of absolute power and absolute servitude!

Noah nodded, a slow, thoughtful gesture that acknowledged the weight of the pledge. The bloody purple flames of his Haki had receded, drawn back into the furnace of his heart, leaving his presence less overtly terrifying but somehow more dense, more potent.
His gaze was sharp, analytical, the eyes of a being who saw existence as a grand, intricate puzzle.
"What can you tell us about THE Living Emotive?" he asked, his voice a calm, steady current in the sea of ambient power.
Malphas performed a somber bow, a gesture of profound respect for both his new Master and the memory of his old one.
"I do not remember too much, My Lord" he began, his cultured baritone laced with an ancient, lingering sorrow.
"My existence is... fragmented. But some things, some feelings, are too powerful to be erased completely."

He straightened, his crimson eyes looking past Noah, into a time and place that no longer was. "THE Living Emotive was an existence that, true to their name, felt every emotion tremendously. More than any being could ever realize. For them, joy was not a feeling, but a state of being that could illuminate entire Folds. Sorrow was not an emotion, but a weight that could make spacetime itself weep."
The others gathered on the Shore...Sigrid, Moiraine, Ruination, and the Infiniverse, drew closer, their own immense powers held in check as they listened.

"But this sensitivity was a double-edged blade," Malphas continued, his voice heavy. "When the other Living Existences, in their arrogance or ignorance, put them down... their negative emotions amplified. I remember a time when THE Living Dimensional mocked them, saying emotions were just the 'foam on the ocean, not the ocean itself.' THE Living Emotive simply smiled and walked away, but I felt it. The Everything of their Shame and Rage began to swell, to boil. If it were unleashed, it would not have been a storm; it would have been an apocalypse of feeling, a wave of pure despair that could have drowned quintillions of consciousnesses."
He paused, letting the weight of that sink in.

"To prevent this, to protect existence from the sheer, overwhelming force of their own heart, THE Living Emotive took on Servants. We became vessels. They would give us their Everythings of negative emotions, pouring their Hatred, their Fear, their Sorrow, their Cruelty into us, until they could find their balance again."

chapters.title: Chapter 4201 Powerful! V
paragraphs: Noah's gaze was calm, but a universe of calculation was happening behind his eyes.
Beside him, Khor's mysterious eyes narrowed. Servants of THE Living Emotive... her thoughts were a private whisper to Noah as she said..
'I did not know Emotive was doing this.'

Malphas nodded regally, acknowledging their silent contemplation before continuing. "I have one clear memory," he said, his crimson eyes clouding over. "A day when my Master returned to our domain, their entire being a tempest of incandescent fury. Their form was a swirling storm of colors I had never seen before, each one a different flavor of violation and rage."
He took a slow breath, and the scene painted itself in the air from his words.

"'I will not amount to much?!'" Malphas's voice shifted, taking on the resonant, multi-tonal quality of his former master. "'Do they truly not know how much weight I hold?! How much of these Folds I support?! How much of existence would crumble without me to give it meaning, to give it feeling?! Why do they do this?! WHY?!'"
HUUM!
The remembered anguish was so potent that the Radiant Shore itself seemed to dim in sympathy.

"At that time," Malphas said, his own voice returning, "I and the other servants went to them. They were bubbling with negative emotions, on the verge of a cataclysmic release. We knelt, and we did what we were made to do. We opened our own existences, and they began portioning it out. The Everything of their Hatred, a torrent of burning acid, flowed into one of us. The Everything of their Rage, a storm of pure, destructive force, filled another. To me, that day, I received a portion of their Sorrow and their Insecurity."

He touched his own chest, a gesture of profound, remembered pain. "We took it all, until they calmed. Until the storm passed." He looked up, his eyes meeting Noah's. "And when they had calmed, when their form had returned to a state of serene, melancholic beauty, they looked at us, their loyal vessels, and said something I will never forget." His voice dropped to a chilling whisper.
"'Okay. I will show them. I. Will. Show.'"
BOOM!
The words hung in the air, a promise of vengeance so cold and so absolute it made the warmth of the Shore feel like a lie.
Noah looked at Malphas, his eyes shining with a tyrannical light. "What did THE Living Emotive plan?"

Malphas bowed, his form a perfect expression of regretful ignorance. "I do not truly know, Master. But if you are suspicious whether THE Living Emotive had a hand to play in what is coming... I can decisively say..." He raised his head, his crimson eyes holding a universe of terrible possibility.
"Maybe."
BOOM!
The word was another detonation, another piece of a puzzle so vast and so terrifying that it threatened to overwhelm all other concerns.
Malphas's expression softened, a deep, abiding respect coloring his features. "My Master was not a monster," he said, his voice a soft, mournful defense.

"They were graceful, kind. They treated us, their servants, with a respect that the other Living Existences rarely showed to anyone. But their power... their power was different. It didn't just affect matter or space. It resonated with all existences. Every being that feels, from the smallest insect to the grandest Creature, is, in some small way, connected to them."

He paused, a terrible, logical conclusion forming on his lips. "They were, I believe, likely the most powerful of all of them, if they had ever lived up to their full potential. Maybe even stronger than the one deemed the strongest... THE Living Paradox. And maybe... maybe that was why the others treated them in such a way. Out of fear."
His gaze became distant, lost in the what-ifs of a forgotten age. "But if my Master did finally snap... if they truly decided to 'show them'... then nothing could stop them."
The words were a death knell. Noah and Khor exchanged a glance, a silent acknowledgment of this new, terrifying variable.
They had been preparing for the Fallout, for the inevitable decline of existence. But what if it wasn't an inevitable, natural process?

What if it had been... orchestrated by a select few? A lesson in suffering, delivered by a being who had been taught that lesson better than anyone else. If they could figure out excatly what was done, aas there a chance to reverse it?
What had THE Living Emotive done? The question was a new, dark star in the constellation of their worries, and its light was cold, and vast, and utterly terrifying!
Jealousy...that delightful emotion that has toppled more empires than war, ruined more relationships than infidelity, and caused more poor decisions than alcohol and online shopping combined.

Consider the hero's party entering a terrifying dungeon. The hero, because this is how these stories always go, is surrounded by beautiful priestesses, mysterious rogues, and various other women who have inexplicably decided that sharing one man between seven of them is a perfectly reasonable arrangement.
They laugh at his jokes (which aren't funny), swoon at his muscles (which aren't that impressive), and generally make the dungeon crawl look like a mobile harem anime.
In the shadows, a lone goblin watches this display.
Now, this goblin had been content with his life...a little stabbing here, some treasure hoarding there, maybe a nice mushroom stew on his off days.
But seeing this mediocre human surrounded by such devotion while he, a goblin with excellent hygiene for his species and a respectable collection of shiny rocks, remained alone?
Jealousy took root.
"That's it," the goblin muttered, adjusting his loincloth with newfound determination. "No more playing around."

We don't need to discuss what happened after that. Let's just say the hero's party learned that a motivated goblin with nothing to lose and everything to prove is significantly more dangerous than a demon lord who's just going through the motions.
But this was hardly the first time jealousy had catastrophic consequences!
In the Earliest Folds, in a memory that existence itself had tried to forget, THE Creature had sat down with THE Living Dimensional in what passed for intervention at that level of being.
"Must you treat THE Living Emotive this way?" THE Creature's voice carried the particular weight of someone trying to prevent a disaster they could see coming from several eons away.
"Just out of your own jealousy?"
THE Living Dimensional snorted...a sound that created three new types of weavings that immediately regretted existing.
"I hate his Way of Existence," THE Living Dimensional said with venom that could have dissolved concepts.

"I hate that without having to do anything, Emotive has all that power. Joy, sorrow, rage, love...they all just flow to him naturally. He doesn't have to calculate dimensions, doesn't have to maintain spatial integrity, doesn't have to work for any of it!"
The bitterness in those words could have curdled time itself.
"And You...You do not need to insert yourself in our matters, O Creature. We are inherently different!"
THE Creature had regarded THE Living Dimensional with something that might have been pity if pity could exist at that scale.

"Different, yes. But that difference isn't what bothers you. What bothers you is that THE Living Emotive's existence makes yours feel like effort. You see his natural state and interpret your own work as inadequacy."
"He doesn't even appreciate what he has!" THE Living Dimensional's form flickered through seventeen impossible geometries in agitation.
"Do you know how much concentration it takes to maintain even basic three-dimensional stability? And he just... feels things into existence!"

"And so your jealousy will poison both your existences," THE Creature observed. "You'll spend eons trying to prove your Way of Existence is superior while he wonders why you seem to hate him for simply being."
"Good."
That single word, delivered with such spite, would echo through existence in ways that wouldn't become apparent until much later.
Jealousy.
Oh, the terrifying things jealousy could bring!

It could make a goblin take down a hero's party. It could make fundamental forces of existence sabotage each other. It could make beings who should be allies become enemies over perceived inequalities that were really just differences.
It was the emotion that whispered, "Why them and not you?"
The feeling that transformed admiration into resentment, respect into rage, appreciation into destruction.
It was perhaps the only force in existence that grew stronger the more you fed it while simultaneously making you hungrier.
Jealousy had probably killed more beings than death itself...at least death was honest about its intentions!

"A day when my Master returned to our domain, their entire being a tempest of incandescent fury.
Their form was a swirling storm of colors I had never seen before, each one a different flavor of violation and rage."
He took a slow breath, and the scene painted itself in the air from his words.
"'I will not amount to much?!'" Malphas's voice shifted, taking on the resonant, multi-tonal quality of his former master.
"'Do they truly not know how much weight I hold?!
How much of these Folds I support?!
How much of existence would crumble without me to give it meaning, to give it feeling?!
Why do they do this?!
WHY?!'"
HUUM!
The remembered anguish was so potent that the Radiant Shore itself seemed to dim in sympathy.
"At that time," Malphas said, his own voice returning, "I and the other servants went to them.
They were bubbling with negative emotions, on the verge of a cataclysmic release.
We knelt, and we did what we were made to do.
We opened our own existences, and they began portioning it out.
The Everything of their Hatred, a torrent of burning acid, flowed into one of us.
The Everything of their Rage, a storm of pure, destructive force, filled another.
To me, that day, I received a portion of their Sorrow and their Insecurity."
He touched his own chest, a gesture of profound, remembered pain.
"We took it all, until they calmed.
Until the storm passed." He looked up, his eyes meeting Noah's.

"And when they had calmed, when their form had returned to a state of serene, melancholic beauty, they looked at us, their loyal vessels, and said something I will never forget." His voice dropped to a chilling whisper.
"'Okay.
I will show them.
I.
Will.
Show.'"
BOOM!
The words hung in the air, a promise of vengeance so cold and so absolute it made the warmth of the Shore feel like a lie.
Noah looked at Malphas, his eyes shining with a tyrannical light.
"What did THE Living Emotive plan?"
Malphas bowed, his form a perfect expression of regretful ignorance.
"I do not truly know, Master.
But if you are suspicious whether THE Living Emotive had a hand to play in what is coming...
I can decisively say..." He raised his head, his crimson eyes holding a universe of terrible possibility.
"Maybe."
BOOM!
The word was another detonation, another piece of a puzzle so vast and so terrifying that it threatened to overwhelm all other concerns.
Malphas's expression softened, a deep, abiding respect coloring his features.
"My Master was not a monster," he said, his voice a soft, mournful defense.
"They were graceful, kind.
They treated us, their servants, with a respect that the other Living Existences rarely showed to anyone.
But their power... their power was different.
It didn't just affect matter or space.
It resonated with all existences.
Every being that feels, from the smallest insect to the grandest Creature, is, in some small way, connected to them."
He paused, a terrible, logical conclusion forming on his lips.
"They were, I believe, likely the most powerful of all of them, if they had ever lived up to their full potential.
Maybe even stronger than the one deemed the strongest...
THE Living Paradox.
And maybe... maybe that was why the others treated them in such a way.
Out of fear."
His gaze became distant, lost in the what-ifs of a forgotten age.
"But if my Master did finally snap... if they truly decided to 'show them'... then nothing could stop them."
The words were a death knell.
Noah and Khor exchanged a glance, a silent acknowledgment of this new, terrifying variable.
They had been preparing for the Fallout, for the inevitable decline of existence.
But what if it wasn't an inevitable, natural process?
What if it had been... orchestrated by a select few?
A lesson in suffering, delivered by a being who had been taught that lesson better than anyone else.
If they could figure out excatly what was done, aas there a chance to reverse it?
What had THE Living Emotive done?
The question was a new, dark star in the constellation of their worries, and its light was cold, and vast, and utterly terrifying!
Jealousy...that delightful emotion that has toppled more empires than war, ruined more relationships than infidelity, and caused more poor decisions than alcohol and online shopping combined.
Consider the hero's party entering a terrifying dungeon.

The hero, because this is how these stories always go, is surrounded by beautiful priestesses, mysterious rogues, and various other women who have inexplicably decided that sharing one man between seven of them is a perfectly reasonable arrangement.
They laugh at his jokes (which aren't funny), swoon at his muscles (which aren't that impressive), and generally make the dungeon crawl look like a mobile harem anime.
In the shadows, a lone goblin watches this display.
Now, this goblin had been content with his life...a little stabbing here, some treasure hoarding there, maybe a nice mushroom stew on his off days.
But seeing this mediocre human surrounded by such devotion while he, a goblin with excellent hygiene for his species and a respectable collection of shiny rocks, remained alone?
Jealousy took root.
"That's it," the goblin muttered, adjusting his loincloth with newfound determination.
"No more playing around."
We don't need to discuss what happened after that.
Let's just say the hero's party learned that a motivated goblin with nothing to lose and everything to prove is significantly more dangerous than a demon lord who's just going through the motions.
But this was hardly the first time jealousy had catastrophic consequences!
In the Earliest Folds, in a memory that existence itself had tried to forget, THE Creature had sat down with THE Living Dimensional in what passed for intervention at that level of being.
"Must you treat THE Living Emotive this way?" THE Creature's voice carried the particular weight of someone trying to prevent a disaster they could see coming from several eons away.
"Just out of your own jealousy?"
THE Living Dimensional snorted...a sound that created three new types of weavings that immediately regretted existing.
"I hate his Way of Existence," THE Living Dimensional said with venom that could have dissolved concepts.
"I hate that without having to do anything, Emotive has all that power.
Joy, sorrow, rage, love...they all just flow to him naturally.
He doesn't have to calculate dimensions, doesn't have to maintain spatial integrity, doesn't have to work for any of it!"
The bitterness in those words could have curdled time itself.
"And You...You do not need to insert yourself in our matters, O Creature.
We are inherently different!"
THE Creature had regarded THE Living Dimensional with something that might have been pity if pity could exist at that scale.
"Different, yes.
But that difference isn't what bothers you.
What bothers you is that THE Living Emotive's existence makes yours feel like effort.
You see his natural state and interpret your own work as inadequacy."
"He doesn't even appreciate what he has!" THE Living Dimensional's form flickered through seventeen impossible geometries in agitation.
"Do you know how much concentration it takes to maintain even basic three-dimensional stability?
And he just... feels things into existence!"
"And so your jealousy will poison both your existences," THE Creature observed.
"You'll spend eons trying to prove your Way of Existence is superior while he wonders why you seem to hate him for simply being."
"Good."
That single word, delivered with such spite, would echo through existence in ways that wouldn't become apparent until much later.
Jealousy.
Oh, the terrifying things jealousy could bring!
It could make a goblin take down a hero's party.
It could make fundamental forces of existence sabotage each other.
It could make beings who should be allies become enemies over perceived inequalities that were really just differences.
It was the emotion that whispered, "Why them and not you?"
The feeling that transformed admiration into resentment, respect into rage, appreciation into destruction.
It was perhaps the only force in existence that grew stronger the more you fed it while simultaneously making you hungrier.
Jealousy had probably killed more beings than death itself...at least death was honest about its intentions!

chapters.title: Chapter 4202 Far Too Late! I
paragraphs: Malphas stood before Noah, a regal, obsidian figure against the radiant white-gold backdrop of the Shore, his bearing a perfect paradox of absolute power and absolute servitude.

"My Lord," he began, his cultured baritone a calm, steady note in the symphony of the Shore's ambient power, "I will detail any pertinent memories that come to me and let you know. But since you are fighting against time itself, with a great many unknowns, I will get started in aiding you the best way that I can."
The words were spoken with a conviction so profound it seemed to etch itself into the very air.
Noah gave a light, almost imperceptible nod of assent, an acknowledgment that was all the permission Malphas needed.
Malphas closed his eyes. For a moment, he was perfectly still. Then, from the shadows his own form cast upon the golden sands, two more figures began to rise.

They were not summoned; they were born from the obsidian darkness of his being, a darkness thick and heavy with the screaming silence of a billion negative emotions...the inherited, recycled despair of THE Living Emotive!

Two perfect, identical copies of himself materialized, their crimson eyes opening in perfect synchrony. If any being were to underestimate them, to see them as mere clones, they would not even know how they died!

With a final, deep bow, the three figures of Malphas began to move. One body turned and shot towards the distant, archaic entrance to the Primordial Early Excavation Depths, its form a blur of focused intent.
His Master had only just begun to plumb its secrets; he would continue the work.
Another body simply vanished, flickering out of existence with a speed that left not even a ripple in reality. A second later...
WAP!
He reappeared at the edge of the Shore, but he was not alone!
In his hands, held like inescapable iron clamps, were the massive, grotesque corpses of two Dead Existences.

They were the very same beings that Khor had so casually crumpled and laid at Noah's feet in the ruined Transcendent Origin Folds. Malphas had traveled across the Folds and back in less than a single second, a feat of dimensional traversal that would have left most Dukes bewildered!

He carried the corpses, each one a monument to a different flavor of ending, toward the Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary. The nine young Inevitabilities, still feasting on the last of the Mead, began to wriggle with a new, ravenous glee at the scent of such a profound meal.
Malphas looked at them, his expression stern, his own one quadrillion in Complexity and Purity erupting out in a wave of cold, commanding authority.
"Order," he said, his voice a sharp, cutting command that made even the chaotic natures of the young Inevitabilities pause.
They stilled their writhing, their innocent, stellar obsidian eyes fixing on him with a newfound respect.

They formed a line, a perfect, orderly queue of unfathomable hunger. Malphas nodded once, a gesture of approval. With a wave of his hand, a blade of pure, solidified darkness fell, methodically cutting up one of the corpse into nine equal, mountain-sized portions!
One by one, he distributed the pieces, ensuring a calm, structured feeding. As he did this, he waved his other hand towards the second corpse.
In the next moment, the entire colossal being crumbled into a swirling, obsidian mass of pure, concentrated authority, which he took and swallowed in a single, decisive gulp!
His eyes flashed with a brilliant crimson radiance as his body began to emanate an even grander wave of power, before that body, too, vanished once more.

The original Malphas, who had remained standing before Noah this entire time, bowed once more. "My Lord," he said, his voice as calm and steady as if he had done nothing more than pour a cup of tea, "since I am your servant, I will take care of all the menial tasks for you. For this, you do not have to worry and can focus on other matters. I will give you progress reports every hour, if need be, of any major changes and accomplishments."
WAA!
As he spoke, his bowed figure saw a prompt of verdant, golden light rise before his eyes, its words for him and him alone.

|Your Lord senses the tremendous effort you are putting in. The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest supports you and will elevate all your actions completely. Your Master is looking fondly at your actions. Keep it up to become the best possible servant.|
Malphas saw this, and his crimson eyes flashed with a glorious, all-consuming ambition to serve!
For he was a servant!
And hus previous Master alone...was THE Living Emotive!
Far away, in the Transcendent Spirit Folds, the very concept of reality was a gentle, flowing thing.
Here, in an area filled with the weavings of white rivers of brilliance and pure spirituality, there was nothing but a serene, endless expanse of light. But at this moment, that peace was shattered.
A massive Tear opened, a jagged, necrotic wound in the pristine fabric of the spiritual plane. It was a violation, a scream of wrongness in a place that had only ever known a quiet hum!
While the Tears of Existence were blooming with alarming frequency in the Origin Folds, it did not mean they were occurring only there.
With less frequency, for now, they were beginning to appear across all the Folds.
What was unique about this particular tear was the region it had chosen to violate. This was the domain now under the quiet, pervasive influence of... The Great Usurper.
His consciousness was an invisible atmosphere, a cloud of pure awareness that other existences could not perceive.
At this moment, in the depths of that consciousness, prompts bloomed.
|A Tear of Existence, a rupture in The Veil, has occurred in the region of the Transcendent Spirit Folds currently under your influence.|

The Great Usurper's idle, drifting thoughts sharpened into a stern, serious focus. In the next moment, he felt his own terrifying power tremble, as if the very presence of the tear was trying to forcefully dissipate his carefully maintained, scattered existence!

chapters.title: Chapter 4203 Far Too Late! II
paragraphs: And yet, even as this occurred, The Great Usurper took no action.
His gaze remained one of profound, unshakable laziness. He almost wanted to go back to his slumber. He had The Idle Gaming System!
After all these years, he had long since figured out that he simply needed to stay idle.
And surely, in the next moment, another set of prompts rose to meet his serene, inactive will.

|Your influence has begun to thread through the connection between the Transcendent Spirit Folds and the Tear of Existence. Your authority is slowly permeating across the weavings of reality to begin flowing into the torn Veil.|

|An infinitesimal amount of The Veil is gradually falling under your influence. Future potential effects are unknown, but the immediate effect is an increase in Idle Loot, with new selections now possible.|
The Great Usurper's existence smiled. He pulled up his Idle Gaming System Interface, his attention drawn to the new, glittering possibilities in his loot table.
|New Idle Loot now possible: [Veil Patch] - A small, conceptual patch that can be used to mend tears in reality. May or may not work. Use at your own risk.|
|New Idle Loot now possible: [Essence of a Lost Soul] - A common resource dropped by entities that cross The Veil.|
|New Idle Loot now possible: [Fragment of a Dead Existence's Memory] - A rare drop. May contain useful information or just existential dread...|
He looked at these new possibilities with shining eyes, a silent, amused chuckle rippling through his consciousness.

'How all of this seems foreboding and all,' he thought, 'but my goal is to still remain Idle... Let's see, does that crazy guy know anything about this? If this becomes something that can affect my idle life... hmm.'
With a final, pondering thought, the Great Usurper pulled upon a connection, a silver, shimmering entanglement that stretched across the Folds, a line cast to none other than Osmont.
He wanted an update on what, exactly, was happening to the Folds while he was trying to nap!
Far from The Great Usurper.
In the Transcendent Emotive Folds, there exist regions where feelings are not merely experienced, but are the very substance of reality.
In one such region, a silent, glacial cold reigned. It was a cold that did not freeze water, but hope. A cold that did not crystallize air, but the will to continue.

Here, in this expanse of frozen despair, countless mirrors of glacial white stood scattered like doorways to forgotten memories, each one a perfect, unblemished surface that reflected not light, but the profound emptiness of the space around them.
Rarely would any being give these mirrors a second glance. They were monuments to stillness, fragile things that would shatter into a thousand pieces of crystallized sorrow at the slightest touch.

And yet, at this moment, two figures, wreathed in a faint, protective glow, passed through one of the mirrors as if it were nothing more than a veil of mist. It did not shatter. It rippled, accepting their passage, and then returned to its perfect, frozen state.

Uniquely, for these two, none of the mirrors here would have shattered. They were the key to a lock that had been waiting for eons. On each of their chests, an intricate, nine-pointed star was etched...the Enneagram, spinning with a slow, majestic rhythm.

The moment they passed through, they appeared in a region of even more terrifying cold. The temperature here was a physical assault, a pressure so immense that it could have frozen the very existence of an Honored Living Existence in a matter of seconds, causing their authority to crystallize and then collapse into dust.

But the two were protected. The Enneagrams on their chests were spinning like glorious, silent engines, their light a warm, defiant glow that actively absorbed the crushing, emotional authority of the environment.
For the power here was not elemental; it was purely the authority of feeling, and emotion alone could decimate a being from the inside out.

The woman, Seraphina Valorheart, looked around, her breath a cloud of mist that seemed to contain tiny, frozen sparks. As she felt the steady, protective hum of the treasure on her chest, her gaze shifted to the man beside her.
Alexander Asmodeus. He kept his gaze fixed forward, his handsome face a mask of stern focus.
He had not turned to look at her, not even once, since their... intimacy. Since the moment their Enneagrams had required a connection that transcended the spiritual.
A pang of pain, sharp and cold, pierced her heart, and she did not know it, but the already frigid air around them grew even colder, a reflection of the sorrow she felt.
She looked at him, at the strong, silent line of his jaw, and her voice was a fragile thing, a whisper against the vast silence.

"I know you have another in your heart," she began, the words tasting of a bitter truth she had been forced to swallow. "But you were the one who was intimate with me. The only one. Whether you want to acknowledge it or ignore it, you currently hold my heart in your hands. Will you truly treat me so coldly as to not even look at me?"
HUUM!
Her words pulsed with a raw, vulnerable feeling, a wave of pure emotion sent out into the cold!
Alexander remained still for a long moment, his gaze unwavering. Then, his voice, a low and steady, cut through the silence.
"The reason I am not looking at you is not because I wish to ignore you," he said, his tone devoid of cruelty, yet heavy with a pragmatism that was almost as painful.
"The moment I laid with you was the moment you became mine. You do not have to worry. I will take care of you."
He paused, and the weight of his next words was a physical thing. "The reason I am not looking at you right now is because all around us is unprecedented danger. And you cannot even sense it."
His words struck her with a dual force. Mine. The word was a sunburst in the winter of her heart, a possessive claim that sent a wave of warmth through her.
And yet, the second part of his statement was a chilling reminder of the chasm that separated their perceptions. The joy and the grimness warred within her, a tumultuous storm of feeling!
In the next moment, the glacial white surroundings began to alter. The ground beneath them trembled, and all around, the very substance of the realm began to rise, to form.
Massive white statues, carved from what looked like pure, crystalline marble, erupted from the frozen ground, nine titans of law and judgment rising to surround them!
Law!
It was thr inheritance of THE Living Law, and it bore asking...why the hell it was even in the lands of Emotive!

Massive white statues, carved from what looked like pure, crystalline marble, erupted from the frozen ground, nine titans of law and judgment rising to surround them!
Law!
It was thr inheritance of THE Living Law, and it bore asking...why the hell it was even in the lands of Emotive!

chapters.title: Chapter 4204 Far Too Late! III
paragraphs: Nine massive statues arose all around the Peacemaker and Seraphina!
They were magnificent, terrible things, their muscular forms etched with an eternity of sorrowful judgment, their faces a perfect blend of profound disappointment and deep, paternal sorrow.
Their terrifying white eyes, devoid of pupils, radiated a light of pure, unyielding law.
All nine turned their gaze upon Alexander and Seraphina, a silent, collective judgment that seemed to weigh their very souls.
Then, one of the massive statues began to speak, its voice the sound of mountains grinding, of eons passing.

"You two were supposed to be here many, many years ago. If you had taken the inheritance of THE Living Law at that time, you may have had a chance before being laid to waste in the Fallout of what is coming. But now... you are far, far too late."
HUUM!
The words were heavy, each one a death knell. Alexander's face, once so calm, became a mask of stern resolve. "What do you mean?"
All nine statues of law and judgment looked at him, and another spoke, its voice a chorus of echoing pronouncements.

"All existences that were not granted entry into THE Loom countless eons ago are those destined to fall in the coming collapse and Fallout. THE Living Law left behind an inheritance for those who would nurture parts of its shattered will. You two hold the two major components of that will. Had you been here when you were meant to be, you may have had the chance to cultivate your Law to the extent of gaining the chance to pursue an opportunity for survival. But now, even that chance is gone. Now, there is nothing."
Now there was nothing!
The words were so despotic and numb that one could go mad hearing them!
The statue paused, and the silence it left was more terrifying than any sound.

"You would need, at the very least, a few million years. But based on what we have sensed is occurring out in the Folds... not even a million years will pass before the Fallout. It might be a hundred thousand years, or one thousand years, or even one year... the numbers don't truly matter. Whether it happens tomorrow or a million years from now, you two, and all others present across the Folds at this moment, are doomed."
The words were a final, absolute judgment. Seraphina's face paled, the blood draining from it, her eyes wide with the sheer, existential horror of it all. The collapse of everything. Certain doom!
But the visage of Alexander Asmodeus, the glorious visage of the Peacemaker, shone with an unruly, defiant light.
He looked up at the nine colossal statues, and his voice was a commanding roar that defied their pronouncements of doom.

"I will be the one to make the decision on whether it is too late or not! For now, we came to claim the Tool and the inheritance of THE Living Law. So forget about certain doom and bring it out, so that we may work towards a solution and not wallow in decimation!"
HUUM!

The nine marbled statues looked at him, their cold, sorrowful eyes seeming to gauge the depth of his defiance. Then, as one, they turned back into still, silent stone. The surroundings began to tremble, and their nine synonymous voices echoed out, a final, resigned pronouncement.
"...So be it."
So be it.
Words of cold resignation, but also the words of a possible beginning.
But they were ones sorely needed!
At the same time, in a completely different direction in these very same Transcendent Emotive Folds, space fluctuated.
In a region of murky, obsidian uncertainty, where the air itself was thick with the feeling of doubt and indecision, the figure of Malphas appeared.
His eyes pulsed with a terrifying crimson light. He raised a hand, his movements graceful and deliberate, and his voice rang out, a grand, theatrical proclamation.

"From the many Everythings of Fear and Hatred that I received from my previous Master, I release a portion of them to permeate across these Transcendent Emotive Folds. All the fear and all the hatred of the Living Existences and The Dead Existences within these Folds... shall be transformed to complexity and purity for me and my current Master!"
HUUM!
A terrifying phenomenon occurred. From his hands, two singularities of unfathomable emotion, the very Everythings of THE Living Emotive, surged forth.
They erupted in a silent, terrifying blast of light, one of pure, abject fear, the other of incandescent, all-consuming hatred!
They began to spread, not like a wave, but like a virus, a conceptual plague that infected the very fabric of the Emotive Folds. It was a power too unfathomable for others to even understand.
Prompts, rendered in a verdant, golden light, bloomed before him.

|A tremendous effort is being made, an action of unfathomable weight is being carried out. The resultant effects of this action are further amplified by the Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest.|
|The emotions of Hatred and Fear are particularly abundant in this day and age across the Folds, especially so in the Transcendent Emotive Folds that are ruled by emotion.|
|An initial, preliminary harvesting of all Hatred and Fear has generated One Hundred Trillion in Complexity and Purity that shall be distributed to you and your Master.|
|Hatred and Fear are constant. As they are harvested across the entirety of these Folds, they will be passively collected and distributed once they reach a certain threshold.|
WAA!
An initial harvest. One Hundred Trillion. Ten times the marker of a Duke, and it was just the beginning.
Yet, even as he looked at these heavy, impossible numbers, Malphas frowned. A flicker of disappointment, of impatience, crossed his handsome features.
"Merely 100 Trillion..." he muttered, his voice a low, cruel whisper that was swallowed by the spreading tide of fear and hatred.
As he spoke, another prompt, this one shimmering with a unique, quintessential light, bloomed before his eyes.
|You are well on your way to becoming a Quintessential Servant.|
Yes, he was on his way.
But for Malphas, this was nothing. For his Master, he was just getting started!

chapters.title: Chapter 4205 Way of Existence! I
paragraphs: Malphas gazed around for a fleeting moment, a flicker of something ancient and sorrowful in his crimson eyes, a memory of a time when this place had been a different kind of prison.
Then he shook his head, the memory dissolving like smoke, and disappeared.

When he reappeared, he had crossed countless, impossible distances. He stood in the void of the Transcendent Origin Folds, an unknown number of light-years away from the decimated golden jewel of Aeternitas Concordia.

From here, the devastation was a distant, silent scar on the fabric of existence. He could see the Tears, the gaping, necrotic wounds in reality, and the brilliant, frantic lights of the Living Existences converging around them like antibodies rushing to a mortal wound.
His gaze swept over the battlefield, his perception a scalpel that dissected the chaos.
He saw the newly arrived forces, the strange, verdant glow of the Fold Dwellers from the Wandering Territories, beings who held an excess of one Quadrillion in complexity, just like him.
He saw the furious dance of Nysteria and the nine-headed turtle, a battle that was painting the sky in the colors of genesis and endings!
And yet, as he looked upon all this magnificent, terrible power, he felt nothing but a profound, chilling contempt.
Contempt!

"Ants," the thought was a cold, smooth stone in the river of his consciousness. "All of them. They scurry and fight, puffing up their chests with their trillions and quadrillions, thinking themselves masters of their own destiny. They have no idea. Across existence, beings millions of times more powerful than them have risen and fallen. They build their grand citadels and forge their alliances, all the while ignorant of the fundamental truth: they are nothing more than livestock."
HUUM!
His internal monologue was not rage, but a cold, philosophical certainty.

"They believe their power makes them different from the pigs and cattle of lesser worlds, but it does not. They will live their lives, accumulate their strength, and then one day, without warning, they will find themselves lying before the blade of a butcher, their lives no different."
"Because true power does not simply lie in complexity."
His gaze sharpened, a flicker of something almost proprietary in his crimson eyes.

"Even an Early Creature with 100 Quadrillion in Complexity and Purity would be weaker than My Lord. Because they are empty. They have no cards, no true potential... no Early Veiled Shore. No Infinite Mana. No Khor. No THE Living Order. No... me. Compared to the Lord, they would be nothing. And I... I have to move to rectify this discrepancy."
HUUM!
The air around him warped, and then, with a sound like a thousand crows taking flight at once...
CAA!
His body erupted. Thousands of horror-inducing obsidian crows, each with blazing crimson eyes, burst forth from his form like a flutter of dark feathers.

They did not fly; they melded into the surrounding space, their forms becoming one with the shadows between dimensions, and then they began to spread out, silent and unseen, towards the Heart of Origin and other critical areas across the Folds.
"Spread, unobserved" his thoughts were a cold, precise command.
"Find out all you can for me. Find out what Schrodinger is seeking... and more."
WAA!
|A tremendous effort is being made. You are deploying a surveillance network that will span an entire Transcendent Fold. The quality of this effort is... Quintessential.|
|[The Principle of Perpetual Harvest] has noted your ambition. All intelligence gathered will be amplified, providing not just data, but context and potential future outcomes.|
|You currently hold the place as the most capable servant and butler. Keep up the good work.|
Malphas looked at the prompts with a calm, almost dismissive gaze. He could do more. To make the Lord's life easier as he sought a solution, he would take care of everything!
Feeding and nurturing the Inevitabilities. Nurturing himself. Nurturing the Land Lifeforms Heidrun and Yoshinami. Surveillance. And even... elevating his Lord.
He would do it all.
For he was Malphas.
And he was capable!
With a final, imperceptible flicker of brilliance, he disappeared in a wisp of dark smoke.
In the Early Veiled Shore, Noah stood near the Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary, a strange, beautiful smile on his face.
Khor floated near him, but his gaze was one of distant, profound amazement. Malphas... was undoubtedly efficient.
A detailed set of prompts, a report from his new attendant, flashed before his eyes.
|Your servant, Malphas, has acted.|
|A portion of the Everythings of Fear and Hatred from THE Living Emotive have been unleashed upon the Transcendent Emotive Folds.|
|A preliminary harvest has been collected.|
|Complexity Gained for The Early Creature, Osmont: +50,000,000,000,000 (+50 Trillion)|
|Purity Gained for The Early Creature, Osmont: +50,000,000,000,000 (+50 Trillion)|
|A passive income of existential dread has been established. You will now gain power from the collective suffering of an entire Fold. How delightfully tyrannical.|
Noah finished reading the prompts, a low whistle escaping his lips. "The servant of THE Living Emotive seems to have been a terrifying being."
Beside him, Khor nodded, her expression a mixture of ancient memory and present curiosity.

"Even though I hadn't known that Emotive had entities it continued to give its Everythings of negative emotions to... all of it must have been for a reason. But yes, this is a unique weapon and support for you. It should propel your elevation even faster." She paused, her gaze turning sharp. "But when it comes to what you have recently learned regarding THE Living Emotive... they are not someone as pitiful as they appear."
"Oh?" Noah's eyes rose, waiting.
Khor nodded, beginning to float lazily around the Shore, occasionally reaching out to pet one of the young, adoring Inevitabilities that had gathered around her.

"Out of all the Living Existences, THE Living Emotive was in control of emotions in a manner that others could not even fathom. It could potentially locate anything that was hiding. No matter how an existence conceals itself, emotions and feelings are the one thing they cannot hide. Unless one was a collapsed existence that had no signs of death or life... they would feel. And THE Living Emotive could sense all of that feeling. I was not able to hide from it. Nor could something like THE Creature hide from it."
