chapters.title: Chapter 4215 Weavings of Power! IV
paragraphs: As he performed these impossible feats, a profound realization dawned on him.
He felt his own Complexity and Purity being burned as fuel, yes, but behind that, an endless, inexhaustible ocean was instantly refilling what was lost.
His Infinite Mana. It was acting as a perpetual motion engine for his new Artifice. He could do this forever!

And more. He didn't even have to use his own ambient power. The trillions he had already poured into his Heart, the very Everything of Size he had sacrificed to it...that was now a self-contained, self-regenerating battery.
He could draw on the Heart alone, leaving his own vast reserves untouched.
His gaze swept the battlefield and found a new target. A cluster of Dead Existences that looked like colossal, bony worms, their skeletal forms burrowing through the fabric of space itself.
There were six of them, their complexities ranging from 100 Trillion to a monstrous 700 Trillion!
The Crucible of Quintessence.
Distillation, he wove, his will a fine, silver thread that shot out and pierced the entire cluster.
Their chaotic, necrotic auras, the very thing that defined them as The Dead, were stripped away, pulled back toward him like a fisherman reeling in a net.
For a single, vulnerable moment, they were just raw, directionless Complexity, their primary defense gone.
Resonance, he wove, his second command following instantly. He did not attack them himself. Instead, he amplified the quintessential nature of his own Legion.
The Haki shrouds around Ra'Zan, Ozymandias, and the Ape blazed brighter. Their hunger, their death, their fury...all were made more potent, more absolute.
And they descended upon the now-vulnerable worms like a pack of celestial wolves. The slaughter was swift, efficient, and absolute!
Their corpses were instantly dispatched to the Early Veiled Shore.
|Every Weave cast generates a harvest. The more complex the Weave, the richer the yield.|
|Total Harvest from recent efforts: +150 Trillion Complexity and Purity.|
|Your practice is not just making you stronger; it is making you richer in the very currency of existence.|
|The Crucibles of Tyranny, Infinity, and Quintessence are experiencing accelerated growth due to active use.|
|Their corresponding Towers of Osmont within your Atlas are resonating. Advancement is accelerating.|
The battlefield had fallen into a stunned, momentary quiet.

The Living Existences, who had been scrambling to form coordinated attacks against single, powerful Dead, had just witnessed one being, in the span of a few seconds, single-handedly eliminate threats that would have required the combined might of multiple Dukes!
Duke Elagabalus stared, his mouth slightly agape. Duke Diviticus, her form wreathed in the power of her stolen corpse, looked at him with a new, profound shock.
His power was not just great; it was oppressive, a weight on the battlefield that made their own efforts seem like children's games!
Noah's devilish, flame-wreathed gaze turned and settled on Duke Diviticus. He remembered her, of course. He remembered her attempt to devour him in the Paradoxical Folds.
She did not know it, but she had been marked for death long ago. Today was not her day, but that day would come.
Khor shook her head in amazement and appreciation.

Sigrid, seeing him wipe out the most powerful Dead with such ease, felt her own Heart of Order burn with a fierce, ambitious fire. Through him, through her man... she could establish a new, perfect Order across all of existence!
HUUM!
The lull was broken by the roar of the Ancestral Turtle. Its gaze passed over Noah with suspicion as it bellowed a command to the dazed Living Existences.
"Close the Tears! Stop the tide!"
WAA!
But Noah did not move to close any Tears. He felt the glorious, burning power of his Heart, and his gaze locked onto other powerful Dead Existences emerging in the distance.
He began to utilize the system of Existential Artifice once more.
Why would he close the Tears? Why would he stop the flow of a river that was bringing him an endless supply of priceless loot?
For him...
The harvest had just begun!
The battlefield itself was a canvas of glorious, terrible chaos!

Noah stood at its center, as he had tasted the intoxicating power of his new Existential Artifice, a methodology that transformed his immense, raw power into a set of precise, existence-breaking tools.

He had tested Tyranny, Infinity, and Quintessence, and found them all to be magnificent. But there were many more Crucibles, many more authorities that hummed within his being, demanding to be explored.
His gaze, now burning celestial purple suns, swept across the battlefield.
He saw the great turtle unleashing waves of genesis to cauterize the Tears in reality, its nine heads a symphony of creation against the cacophony of The Dead.
And he saw the endless tide of death still pouring through the remaining wounds in the Fold.
He needed another test subject.
His focus settled on a region where a particularly nasty Tear was birthing horrors.
From it, a creature of pure, conceptual dread was emerging. It was a serpent of bone and shadow, its scales shimmering with a light that suggested they existed in multiple locations at once.
Its complexity was a staggering 900 Trillion, a being that could have toyed with the Mummified Dead Existence he had just shattered earlier!
'Perfect.'
HUUM!
A terrifying stick- the Goad, had bloomed in his hands at some point.
Noah's will was the command once more!
A river of his power flowed into the Ascendran Nodule, his heart's engine thrumming as it ignited...the Crucible of Quantum.

The sensation was different from the others. It was not the crushing weight of Tyranny or the boundless rush of Infinity. It was a feeling of... uncertainty. Of all possibilities existing at once, waiting for an observer to choose.
Superposition, he wove, his will a gentle nudge to the fabric of reality.
In the next instant, he was not one, but a thousand. A thousand identical Noahs, each wreathed in the same bloody purple flames, each holding a spectral Goad, spread out across the battlefield!
They were not clones, not illusions. They were all him, each one a different probability of his location made manifest, each one equally, absolutely real!
The bone serpent faltered, its myriad eyes trying to process an enemy that was both everywhere and nowhere.

It struck out, its fangs dripping with a venom that could poison causality itself, but it struck only one of Noah's forms, which dissolved into a whisper of possibility as the true Noah, a hundred light years away, prepared his next Weave.
Probability Collapse, he commanded, his gaze, now multiplied a thousand-fold, fixing upon the serpent.

He did not attack. He simply... observed. But his observation was now a weapon. He saw the creature's potential futures, a branching tree of a million possibilities. He saw the path where it successfully bit him, the one where it escaped, the one where it coiled and unleashed a torrent of necrotic energy.
And among them, a single, fragile timeline where a flaw in its own chaotic authority caused its existence to momentarily contradict itself.
He chose that one. He observed it with the full, focused weight of his will. And...he made it inevitable.
Oh.
Oh!
HUUM!
The serpent shrieked, a sound of pure, bewildered agony. It had not been attacked, yet it felt its very essence coming undone!
The future Noah had chosen became the present. A tiny, infinitesimal flaw in its being, a one-in-a-billion chance of spontaneous self-negation, became a 100% certainty!

The creature turned on itself, its own power devouring its existence from the inside out. In a silent, horrifying implosion, the 900 Trillion Complexity Dead Existence collapsed into a point of pure, paradoxical light, and then vanished- taken away to his Shore!
Oh!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 4216 Weavings of Power! V
paragraphs: The thousand Noahs folded back into one, a profound, almost chilling understanding settling into his mind.
This was the power of Quantum. Not just to be in many places, but to choose which reality would be the real one.
As he marveled at the terrifying effectiveness of this new methodology, the battle around him began to shift.
The great turtle, its nine heads now blazing with the amplified authority of Noah's Haki and Sigrid's Order, moved with a new, terrible purpose.
Beams of pure Origin, now focused and precise, lanced out across the Fold, striking not only at The Dead, but at the Tears themselves with concentration.
Where the beams hit, reality was rebooted.
The space was returned to its original, pristine state, the memory of the Tear and the death it had brought completely erased!
The arguments between the factions died down, replaced by a grim, unified focus.
Legions of hundreds of thousands of Living Origins, Laws, Quantums, and others, whose individual complexities were less than a trillion, began to work in concert.

They moved not to the front lines, but to the skeletal remains of Concordia. A great, somber quiet fell over them as they began the heartbreaking work of clearing the bodies of their fallen comrades, of cleansing the ground that had been the home of Origins and a few other Living Existences!
It was a scene of profound, collective grief, a reminder that even for them, the cost of this war was measured in friends and family lost.
Noah watched this for a moment, then his focus shifted. He had seen what Existential Artifice could do in battle. But what of its other applications?
His gaze flickered to the Early Veiled Shore.
He stood upon the golden sands of the Radiant Shore, the air here clean and sweet with the scent of impossible growth.
His main body, which had been observing all these events from afar, now became the center of his focus.
He looked out at the vast, beautiful expanse of his domain. The herbs were maturing, the trees were heavy with fruit, the Aquarium teemed with life. It was a paradise, but it could be more!
He began to test the Weaves, not as weapons, but as tools of wonder.
He turned to a plot where the Transcendent Veilmoss was growing, its fronds shimmering in and out of existence. He ignited the Crucible of the Protagonist.
Plot Advancement, he wove, his will a command to the very story of the plant.
Skip the tedious growth phase. We're moving to the harvest.
|You have exerted the Weave of Narrative Acceleration.|
|The Transcendent Veilmoss has decided its character arc has been fulfilled. It is ready for its dramatic conclusion.|
|Maturation: INSTANTANEOUS.|
The moss flared with a brilliant, ethereal light, its growth cycle completing in a single, glorious instant!
It was ready.

Next, he turned his gaze to the Leviathan's Eternum Cage. The Aquarium was a marvel, but its collection was still limited to the Eminent-level creatures it had managed to ensnare. He wanted more. He wanted... Kleos.
He ignited the Crucible of Life, and the Crucible of Spirit.
Sanctuary's Call, he wove, a complex, two-part harmony of authority. He did not bait the waters with his blood; he baited them with a concept.
He wove the very idea of a perfect, ultimate sanctuary, a place of endless food, absolute safety, and profound peace, and cast it like a fishing line across the dimensional boundaries!
|You have cast the Weave of Irresistible Sanctuary.|
|This conceptual bait is now propagating across adjacent Folds, whispering promises of paradise to all Marine Life.|
|High-level entities are notoriously cautious, but even they are not immune to the promise of a perfect home.|
|A Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeform has taken the bait.|
|Incoming...|
A golden fishing line, one of the Cage's own constructs, snapped taut with a force that made the entire Shore hum.
Something vast and powerful was being hauled across the dimensions, something that had heard his call and found it too compelling to resist.
He smiled, a deep, profound satisfaction filling him!
But his work was not done. His gaze settled on the Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest.
It was a source of unbelievable power, but he knew it could be more.
He ignited...the Crucible of Infinity.
THUMP!
His Heart beat heavily. The Ascendran Nodule beat heavily!
This would take more than a gentle Weave; it would require a torrent of his power, a great and terrible cost!
His existence blazed, hundreds of trillions of Complexity and Purity pouring from his Heart into this single, monumental effort.
He was not just accelerating the Seed's growth; he was using the Weave of Expansion to multiply the very effort the Seed was already exerting, creating a recursive loop of exponential maturation!
HUUM!
His body trembled under the strain, the Shore itself resonating with the sheer, overwhelming power he was unleashing. He felt a deep, conceptual exhaustion, a weariness that went beyond the physical.
His Heart, that raging furnace of Tyranny, began to ache, a warning that even its power had limits.
But he pushed.
|You are performing an act of monumental, reckless effort.|
|You are attempting to force the maturation of a Principle.|
|[The Weave of Infinite Effort Multiplication] is active.|
|The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest is... receptive.|
BOOM!
A wave of verdant, golden light exploded from the Seed, washing over the entire Shore, over the entire Infiniverse!
It was a light so rich, so full of the promise of endless bounty, that it felt like being drowned in pure, liquid hope.
Noah staggered, his body finally reaching its limit. He came to a halt, a deep, profound exhaustion settling into his very Existences!
His Heart needed to rest.
But as he stood there, catching his breath, his Infinite Mana surging to replenish and reenergize his Complexity and Purity used as fuel... the prompts bloomed, and they were worth the cost.
|Every Weave cast generates a harvest. The more complex the Weave, the richer the yield.|
|Total Harvest from recent efforts: +250 Trillion Complexity and Purity.|
|[The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest] has reached 50% Maturity.|
|For a short period of time, the Seed will be resistant to further forced elevation. It must now grow naturally.|
|At 50% Maturity, your connection to the Principle has deepened. You are now capable of forging up to 50 Seed Glyphs of Perpetual Harvest.|
|Cost per Glyph has been elevated to: 100 Trillion Complexity and Purity.|
|Effect per Glyph: The effects of all Weaves and Endowments are now amplified by an unknown factor. Could be 10, could be 100.|
WAA!
He observed and analyzed these terrifying effects, a slow, devilish smile spreading across his face.
Had he...become unfair enough yet?!
The cost was immense, but the returns were astronomical. And as he stood there, basking in the afterglow of his achievement, he took a moment to observe his own, transformed existence.
|Noah Osmont - The Early Creature, Osmont (Age 1)|
|Complexity: (1.8 Quadrillion)|
|Purity: (1.8 Quadrillion)|
|Systems of Power: Early Atlas of the Folds, Infinite Mana, Glyphs, Principles, Existential Artifice (The Weavings of Power)...|
|Distinctions: The Early Creature, Osmont; True Emperor of Quintessence, Tyranny, Infinity; The Living Existential Guider; Master Chef of the Verdant Eternia Tribe...|
|Heart: The Heart of Tyranny (Fourth Part: The Ascendran Nodule - 27% Complete)|
|Principle Access: Perpetual Harvest (50% Matured Seed|
He had gloriously done it.
He had taken a battlefield that Schrodinger likely initiated and turned it into a forge.
He had taken a moment of crisis and turned it into a crucible for his own evolution!

The path ahead was still long, the threat of the Fallout still loomed, but for the first time in a while, he felt like he was returning to a level of terrifying magisterial control and power in a field where he had been weaker than many!

chapters.title: Chapter 4217 Feasts and Festivals! I
paragraphs: The battlefield in the Transcendent Origin Folds was a distant, silent storm on the horizon of Noah's perception, a problem for another version of himself.
Here, in the serene, golden light of the Radiant Shore, a different kind of harvest was underway.
His gaze, no longer titanic in scale but still carrying the weight of more than a Quadrillion, shifted from the contemplative quiet of his own thoughts to the vibrant, chaotic life of his domain.
He turned his attention to the Leviathan's Eternum Cage.

Within the crystalline walls of the Aquarium, a new prisoner raged. It was the Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeform his Weave had ensnared, a creature of the deep, dark places between Folds where light was a forgotten myth!

It was a type of abyssal fish, its body a masterpiece of evolutionary brutality. Its scales were like overlapping plates of polished obsidian, and its eyes were baleful, crimson lanterns that burned with a furious, maddened light.
It smashed its colossal head against the Cage's authority-laced walls again and again, each impact a silent detonation of pure, frustrated power.
Noah watched its futile struggle, a faint, predatory smile touching his lips as he reviewed its details.
|Kleos-Tier Abyssal Anguish Fish|
|Classification: Early Living Marine Lifeform|
|Complexity: 100,000,000,000,000 (100 Trillion)|
|Distinctions:|
|- Child of the Sacred Sea: As a being that has swum in the Early Sacred Waters of a Radiant Shore, its flesh is saturated with an unprecedented concentration of pure, untainted potential.|
|- Embodiment of Rage: Its existence is a constant, burning fire of anger. This makes its flesh particularly potent for those seeking to fuel their own Haki or martial prowess.|
|- A Meal Fit for a King: The consumption of this creature's essence is a monumental undertaking that promises a harvest of unimaginable proportions.|
Noah's eyes shone with a cold, appreciative light.
He had worked hard. He had faced down impossibility, danced on the knife's edge of cessation, and emerged stronger!
Now, it was time for a reward. He ignited the Crucible of...Apocalypse, a True Source that understood the art of endings better than most.
He raised a single finger, and wove.
Sever.
HUUUM!
|You have exerted the Weave of Absolute Severance.|
|The concept of 'connection' is being temporarily negated for the target.|
The Anguish Fish, mid-ram against the wall, froze.
A single, infinitesimally thin line of pure, conceptual blackness appeared across its colossal body.
It was not a cut; it was a statement.

A declaration that the parts of its body were no longer a cohesive whole! In the next instant, the creature fell apart into a few hundred perfectly sliced, still-twitching pieces, its life instantly, cleanly severed.
WAA!
|A Kleos-Tier Lifeform has been... processed. Your efficiency is noted.|
|The effort required was minimal, but the result is a bounty. [The Principle of Perpetual Harvest] is pleased.|
With a wave of his hand, the hundreds of pieces of meat floated out of the Aquarium, hovering in the air before him.
His gaze drifted back to the Cage, to the dozens of Eminent Marine Lifeforms now clustered together in a corner, trembling with a primal, existential terror.
He offered them a devilish, reassuring smile that did not reassure them at all.
He looked at the floating pieces of the Kleos Lifeform, each one a testament to his power, each one a promise of further growth.
He had been so focused on the struggle, on the desperate climb, that he had almost forgotten something fundamental.

After working so hard, one needed to enjoy existence itself. Otherwise, what was the point? If the Fallout did come, if existence itself was to be unmade, he would not meet that end having only known the struggle.
He and those he shouldered the responsibility for would not simply die while struggling. In the struggle, they had to have some enjoyment!
They had to.
So...
He pulled upon the Crucible of Cooking.
Manifest, he wove.
From the golden sands, a massive cooking station erupted, a glorious, impossible structure of obsidian and gold.

It had a cutting board carved from a single, solidified concept of 'sharpness,' a series of grills whose flames could be tuned to the precise temperature of a dying Wheel or the gentle warmth of a summer's day, and a vast, golden basin that hummed with an expectant energy.

With a gesture, he drew the Early Sacred Waters from the nearby sea, a shimmering, cerulean river that flowed through the air and into the basin, instantly beginning to simmer with a gentle, life-giving heat!
He began to cook!
The pieces of the Kleos fish, guided by his will, danced through the air, some searing on the grills, others poaching gently in the Sacred Waters.
The aroma that began to fill the Shore was a thing of pure, celestial beauty, a scent that promised a feast beyond all imagination.
As he worked, a figure approached, her movements hesitant.
It was Sigrid. She had a difficult expression on her face, her eyes holding a familiar, painful emotion: helplessness.
Noah looked at her, and he knew. He knew that even with her newfound few Trillion complexity power, she felt small in the face of the cataclysm unfolding in her home Fold.
He knew the frustration of having immense power yet being unable to solve the one problem that mattered most. He didn't need to hear her ask.
Sometimes, emotional intelligence was more important than anything else, though he wouldn't call himself an expert even now!
So even without waiting for her to say anything...
He simply spoke, his voice a commanding, yet gentle, balm on her unvoiced pain.
"Turn all the decimated Dead Existences I just took down into nutrients for THE Living Order."
Her eyes widened. She turned, and in a distant corner of the Shore, she saw them...the crumpled, broken bodies of the Dead Existences ranging from 100-900 Trillion Noah had personally decimated!
As she watched, the golden sands of the Shore rose, a hungry, shimmering tide that devoured them whole.
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4218 Feasts and Festivals! II
paragraphs: A moment later, Sigrid was bathed in a torrent of pure, golden light, a river of power flowing directly into her being.
|The essence of multiple Dead Existences is being converted into nutrients for THE Living Order.|
|Complexity Gained: +50 Trillion per second.|
|Purity Gained: +50 Trillion per second.|
|This infusion will continue until the threshold of 1 Quadrillion is reached, or the nutrients deplete.|
WUU!
Sigrid stood in the pillar of light, her eyes showing a complex storm of emotions...determination, gratitude, and a love so profound it was its own form of power.
She came to Noah, stood on her toes, and pressed a soft kiss to his forehead.
"Thank you," she whispered.
He smiled. "Focus on your elevation."
She sat down beside him as he continued to cook, her form a serene, glowing beacon of burgeoning power.

Khor floated over, her abyssal eyes looking him up and down with a new, analytical light. "Many beings obtain power and keep it all to themselves," she mused, her voice a philosophical hum. "Because why not? That is a common Way of Existence. But you do the opposite. You are an interesting character, Outsider."
Noah simply nodded with a smile, his focus on the culinary masterpiece he was creating.
His Cooking Tower of Osmont had reached the Third Stage. In addition to bis achievements im the Verdant Eternia Tribe of the Earliest Folds...he could cook...concepts!
And in this moment of crisis, of uncertainty, of a looming, existential doom, he knew exactly what concept needed to be on the menu.
Desperation!
He reached into the very heart of that feeling, the one that had been his constant companion, his most potent fuel.
He pulled upon its essence and wove it into the meat.
The air shimmered, and a new color, a deep, vibrant crimson like the heart of a dying star, flowed down from his hands and into the sizzling fish.
It was the color of the final stand, of the will to fight when all is lost.
For the first time, a concept was being cooked in the Early Veiled Shore!
The process completed with a final, glorious sizzle.
The meat was a work of art, each of the few hundred pieces a perfect, bite-sized jewel.
It was seared to a golden-brown on the outside, the flesh within a pearlescent, translucent white that seemed to glow with its own inner light.
The aroma was a paradox of savory, oceanic notes and something else, something that smelled like... urgency. Like the moment before a storm breaks.
|You have cooked a Concept. This is an act of profound, almost absurd, effort.|
|The resulting dish is a masterpiece that transcends mere food.|
|[The Principle of Perpetual Harvest] is... very impressed.|
|Feast of Desperate Transcendence|
|Effect: Each piece consumed grants +5 Trillion in Complexity and Purity.|

|Conceptual Flavor - Desperation: For one month, the consumer's existence will feel a constant sense of calm urgency and desperation. This state will cause their Complexity and Purity to rise 10 times as quickly through any action.|
|Additional Boon: This meal will permanently increase the consumer's resilience to existential pressure and Haki.|
Oh!

Noah read the prompts as a slow, triumphant smile spread across his face. He looked at the few hundred pieces of perfectly cooked, concept-infused meat floating before him, and then he raised his voice, his command a joyous, booming invitation that echoed across the entire Shore.
"It is time for a feast!"
HUUM!
His voice spread far and wide.
His mother, Moiraine, Titano, the Emperor Penguin, Liora... all came.
His Queens- Barbatos, Adelaide, Athena, and the others, sent forth their clones from the Abode.
This would be the first full feast where his people, his family, would eat a cooked concept.
None of them knew how long they had until the Fallout came. Until then, they had to be desperate. And every now and then... they had to enjoy existence!
They gathered on the golden sands, a glorious, chaotic assembly of titans and monsters.
There were no tables, no fine cutlery. They sat on the ground, a tribal, archaic gathering that felt more real, more honest, than any formal banquet!
Noah motioned with his hands, and a piece of the celestial meat floated to each of them.
They took their first bites. And their eyes opened with a glorious, unified shock.
The taste was a symphony, a story of the deep sea and the burning heart of desperation!
They began to eat in earnest, mouthful after glorious mouthful. Sparkling auroras of pure complexity and purity erupted around each of them, their power levels surging.
Those who were not yet Dukes began their inexorable climb toward the 10 Trillion marker
Soon, all those in the Early Veiled Shore would be Dukes at a minimum!
This... was his power. This was his Tyranny!
It was an archaic feast, a scene of communal power and shared joy that might have been plucked from the memory of the Earliest Folds itself.
And at its center, Noah watched, a quiet, tyrannical patriarch, his heart full, his resolve absolute.
The feast was a symphony of glorious, chaotic joy.

The Radiant Shore was alive with a vibrancy that transcended mere celebration. At its heart, Noah's people, his family, were partaking in a meal that was not just food, but a sacrament of their shared, impossible journey!
Malphas moved among them, a silent, graceful specter of perfect servitude.
Around him, a dozen archaic glasses, carved from what looked like solidified shadow, floated in a perfect, rotating orbit.
They were filled with the Sacred Mead of Existence, a liquid starlight that pulsed with a gentle, white-gold light.
With a flick of his wrist, a glass would detach from the orbit and float to a guest, refilling their cup before they even knew it was empty.
With every sip, their complexity exploded, their very beings humming with a power that was both a gift and a promise.
In a quieter corner, surrounded by a fortress of floating books, the Queen of Matter and the Shadow Guard, Night, were enjoying the feast in their own particular way.

The Queen of Matter had a piece of the concept-infused fish in one hand and a golden quill in the other, her eyes wide with the frantic energy of someone trying to document a miracle while simultaneously experiencing it.
Night, a calm shadow in the brilliant light, would occasionally offer a quiet, insightful comment, a cool counterpoint to the Queen's explosive enthusiasm.

Noah watched them all, a quiet, profound satisfaction settling deep within the furnace of his Heart of Tyranny. He saw his mother, her face radiant with a power that now matched her boundless love, laughing with Adelaide and Athena!

sentences.text: A moment later, Sigrid was bathed in a torrent of pure, golden light, a river of power flowing directly into her being.
|The essence of multiple Dead Existences is being converted into nutrients for THE Living Order.|
|Complexity Gained: +50 Trillion per second.|
|Purity Gained: +50 Trillion per second.|
|This infusion will continue until the threshold of 1 Quadrillion is reached, or the nutrients deplete.|
WUU!
Sigrid stood in the pillar of light, her eyes showing a complex storm of emotions...determination, gratitude, and a love so profound it was its own form of power.
She came to Noah, stood on her toes, and pressed a soft kiss to his forehead.
"Thank you," she whispered.
He smiled.
"Focus on your elevation."
She sat down beside him as he continued to cook, her form a serene, glowing beacon of burgeoning power.
Khor floated over, her abyssal eyes looking him up and down with a new, analytical light.
"Many beings obtain power and keep it all to themselves," she mused, her voice a philosophical hum.
"Because why not?
That is a common Way of Existence.
But you do the opposite.
You are an interesting character, Outsider."
Noah simply nodded with a smile, his focus on the culinary masterpiece he was creating.
His Cooking Tower of Osmont had reached the Third Stage.
In addition to bis achievements im the Verdant Eternia Tribe of the Earliest Folds...he could cook...concepts!
And in this moment of crisis, of uncertainty, of a looming, existential doom, he knew exactly what concept needed to be on the menu.
Desperation!
He reached into the very heart of that feeling, the one that had been his constant companion, his most potent fuel.
He pulled upon its essence and wove it into the meat.
The air shimmered, and a new color, a deep, vibrant crimson like the heart of a dying star, flowed down from his hands and into the sizzling fish.
It was the color of the final stand, of the will to fight when all is lost.
For the first time, a concept was being cooked in the Early Veiled Shore!
The process completed with a final, glorious sizzle.
The meat was a work of art, each of the few hundred pieces a perfect, bite-sized jewel.
It was seared to a golden-brown on the outside, the flesh within a pearlescent, translucent white that seemed to glow with its own inner light.
The aroma was a paradox of savory, oceanic notes and something else, something that smelled like... urgency.
Like the moment before a storm breaks.
|You have cooked a Concept.
This is an act of profound, almost absurd, effort.|
|The resulting dish is a masterpiece that transcends mere food.|
|[The Principle of Perpetual Harvest] is... very impressed.|
|Feast of Desperate Transcendence|
|Effect: Each piece consumed grants +5 Trillion in Complexity and Purity.|
|Conceptual Flavor - Desperation: For one month, the consumer's existence will feel a constant sense of calm urgency and desperation.
This state will cause their Complexity and Purity to rise 10 times as quickly through any action.|
|Additional Boon: This meal will permanently increase the consumer's resilience to existential pressure and Haki.|
Oh!
Noah read the prompts as a slow, triumphant smile spread across his face.

He looked at the few hundred pieces of perfectly cooked, concept-infused meat floating before him, and then he raised his voice, his command a joyous, booming invitation that echoed across the entire Shore.
"It is time for a feast!"
HUUM!
His voice spread far and wide.
His mother, Moiraine, Titano, the Emperor Penguin, Liora... all came.
His Queens- Barbatos, Adelaide, Athena, and the others, sent forth their clones from the Abode.
This would be the first full feast where his people, his family, would eat a cooked concept.
None of them knew how long they had until the Fallout came.
Until then, they had to be desperate.
And every now and then... they had to enjoy existence!
They gathered on the golden sands, a glorious, chaotic assembly of titans and monsters.
There were no tables, no fine cutlery.
They sat on the ground, a tribal, archaic gathering that felt more real, more honest, than any formal banquet!
Noah motioned with his hands, and a piece of the celestial meat floated to each of them.
They took their first bites.
And their eyes opened with a glorious, unified shock.
The taste was a symphony, a story of the deep sea and the burning heart of desperation!
They began to eat in earnest, mouthful after glorious mouthful.
Sparkling auroras of pure complexity and purity erupted around each of them, their power levels surging.
Those who were not yet Dukes began their inexorable climb toward the 10 Trillion marker
Soon, all those in the Early Veiled Shore would be Dukes at a minimum!

chapters.title: Chapter 4219 Feasts and Festivals! III
paragraphs: He saw Titano, the simple giant, being shown by Erikson how to properly hold a piece of fish with a slipper for maximum comedic effect.
He saw his son, Henry, standing with Liora, as the two ate.
He saw it all, and he knew this moment of peace, this fragile island of joy in an ocean of impending doom, could not last.
It was time.
He rose, and the joyous din of the feast quieted. All eyes turned to him, their gazes filled with a mixture of reverence, loyalty, and a deep, abiding trust.
"We have been through many things together," he began, his voice a calm, steady current that flowed across the golden sands.
"We have faced apocalypses, battled monsters, and stood against forces that should have unmade us. We have survived. And we have grown stronger for it."
HUUM!
He let the words hang in the air, a shared acknowledgment of their impossible journey!

"Recently," he continued, his tone shifting, the warmth in his voice giving way to a cold, hard gravity, "I learned of events that occurred eons ago, in the Earliest Folds. Events that set into motion the collapse of Existence itself. A coming Fallout."
A hush fell over the crowd. The food, moments before a source of ecstatic pleasure, suddenly felt heavy in their hands.

"The stories you have begun to hear about THE Living Existences, about THE Creature... all those beings are supposedly protected in a bunker of their own making. Everyone else, everyone outside of this bunker, of this... Loom... is destined to perish."
BOOM!

The words were a quiet detonation, a truth so vast and so terrible it seemed to suck the very air from the Shore. Many paused mid-chew, their eyes wide and bright as they listened, the taste of desperation from the meal now a chilling premonition.

"All of this was set in motion eons ago," Noah's voice was a flat, unyielding line. "Even those who built the bunker did not know when this would occur. It did not happen in the past millions of years. It may not occur in another million years. Or... it could occur in the next year, the next month, or even tomorrow. Nobody knows. And herein lies the reason for our desperation. Why the food you are feasting on is filled with the Concept of Desperation. Because since we do not know when the collapse and the Fallout are coming, we have to do everything we can to attain enough power to survive it."
An immense silence followed, a quiet so profound that the gentle lapping of the Sacred Waters on the distant shore sounded like a roar.
His people gazed at him, and in their eyes, he saw no fear, no despair. Only a shining, unwavering faith.
A faith that was a heavier burden than any crown.
He sighed, the weight of their trust a physical thing upon his shoulders, and he turned his gaze to his son. To Henry.
He looked at him, and then at all of them.

"We have survived many things before this," he said, his voice softer now, laced with a vulnerability. "But the ordeal ahead is one that even I... am unsure of. The power we need to attain is a distant, almost mythical thing. It is not a Power, but THE Power. If we have time, we will achieve it. And that is the only peril...not knowing how much time we have. But until then... we continue to be desperate. We continue to struggle."
He took a breath, his gaze sweeping over each of them, a leader seeing not just soldiers, but family.

"I tell you this situation not to foster fear, but to let you know that I will be doing everything I can. But that is me, in this vastness of existence. Each of you has your own existence. There is no harm in being desperate yourselves... in going as far as you possibly can. Just like any other apocalypse... we will survive this. We will do... whatever it takes."
HUUM!
Whatever it takes. The words were a vow, a promise, a declaration of war against fate itself!
In the silence that followed, a single, defiant figure rose.
The Emperor Penguin, a piece of celestial fish still held in its flipper, raised its other flipper high in the air and bellowed, its voice a comical, yet profoundly serious, squawk.
"WHATEVER IT TAKES!"
For a moment, there was just that single, absurd voice.
Then, another joined. Erikson, a wild grin on his face, rose and raised the Slipper of Existential Humiliation. "Whatever it takes!"
Then Kazuhiko, his hand on his sword, a silent, deadly promise in his eyes. Moiraine, a quiet, burning loyalty in her paradoxical gaze. Titano, a simple, booming echo of his new Brother's will.

Ruination, her voice the sound of endings choosing to fight. The Infiniverse, a chorus of countless souls speaking as one. One by one, they all began to rise, their individual voices a dissonant, chaotic chorus of defiance.
And then, in a few seconds, they found their harmony. They all spoke as one, their unified voice a thunderous, wheel-shaking roar.
"WHATEVER IT TAKES!"
BOOM!
An electrical energy, a current of pure, unadulterated fervor, surged across the Shore!
Khor, who had been watching with shining, ancient eyes, smiled and joined in, her voice a whisper that was somehow the loudest of all.
In the Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary, the young Inevitabilities raised their tentacles and screeched, a hungry, joyous cry of agreement.

Heidrun and Yoshinami appeared, their eyes blazing with a fierce, protective light. Malphas, who had been observing with a profound, respectful gaze, looked at his Lord and mouthed the words, his loyalty a silent, unbreakable oath!
Noah felt it all, their booming shouts, their collective, desperate will. A tidal wave of emotion!

And he did not fight them. He let them wash over him, through him. The bloody purple flames of his Haki, which had been a controlled, contained fire, erupted from him, a raging, regal inferno that reached for the heavens.
He opened his mouth, and his voice, the voice of their Emperor, their leader, their family, joined theirs.
The entire Radiant Shore, every being, every grain of sand, every drop of water, roared as one.
"WHATEVER IT TAKES!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4220 Feasts and Festivals! IV
paragraphs: The Shore buzzed with a glory so profound it seemed to shake the very foundations of existence.
|A moment of Quintessential Unity has been achieved.|
|The collective will of all beings within the Radiant Shore has synchronized with the will of its Master.|
|The effort of this unified declaration has been recognized by [The Principle of Perpetual Harvest].|
|Boon of Unity: For the next 24 hours, all actions taken in service of the collective goal of survival will have their effectiveness amplified by 10,000%.|
|New Distinction Gained: The Tyrant of a Desperate People.|
The echoes of their roar faded, but the energy remained, a palpable, thrumming presence in the air.
Noah gazed out at his people, at their shining eyes, at their faces etched with a singular, terrible purpose.
They would survive. No matter what it took!
Festivals and feasts...these were humanity's answer to the crushing weight of existence.
If you're going to live in existence that might end at any moment- electric shocks, trucks, weapons of mass destruction...you might as well have good food and decent company while you wait!
It's the philosophy of the terminally optimistic or the wisely resigned, depending on your perspective.
They say the purpose of festivals is to celebrate, to mark occasions, to bring communities together.
But really, they're existence's way of saying, "Look, I know everything is temporary and probably meaningless, but have you tried these canapés?"
But really, they're existence's way of saying, "Look, I know everything is temporary and probably meaningless, but have you tried these canapés?"
In the Earliest Folds, when celebration hadn't yet learned to be cautious, one of the largest Festivals of Existence unfolded under the watch of Gilgamesh, The First Leader.
This wasn't some minor gathering where Early Creatures awkwardly mingled while avoiding eye contact.
This was an event so significant that even THE Living Existences descended from whatever lofty dimensions they usually occupied.
THE Living Spirit, THE Living Dimensional, THE Living Elemental, and THE Living Concept floated above the festivities like constellations that had decided to attend a party.
Their forms cast light that didn't follow physics, creating an atmosphere where impossible things seemed merely improbable.
Below them, the festival sprawled across dimensions. Early Creatures whose power could reshape reality mingled with Living Existences still figuring out their authorities.
Even a few Fold Dwellers had been invited...or had invited themselves; the records were unclear on that point.
At the center of it all, Gilgamesh sat upon a grand white throne that made mountains feel inadequate.

He received a procession of Early Creatures fro different Tribes paying respects, each one approaching with gifts that would have bankrupted civilizations—compressed Wheels, crystallized time, concepts that had been considered too dangerous to exist.

The surviving Early Creatures that had been a part of the Verdant Eternia Tribe had outdone themselves among those cooking. They had advanced their cooking methodology to the point where flavor transcended taste and became experience.
One bite of their prepared dishes could convey entire lifetimes of satisfaction. Sacred Herbs that normally required eons to mature had been cultivated specifically for this event.
It was, by all accounts, harmonious. Which should have been everyone's first warning.
A jubilant cloud of emotions descended from above...not gradually but with the suddenness of feelings that refuse to be ignored.
THE Living Emotive had arrived, fashionably late to a party that hadn't invited them.

The reaction from the other THE Living Existences was immediate and unwelcoming. THE Living Dimensional's form contracted with visible disgust, its voice carrying across dimensions with deliberate clarity.
"You are not welcome here, Emotive. This festival has no need of your... particular contributions."
The public rejection, spoken before countless witnesses, would have devastated any being that cared about social standing.
THE Living Emotive simply smiled wider, emotions cycling through its form like a kaleidoscope of feeling.
"Without emotions, how can there be a feast?" Emotive's voice carried forced cheer that made several nearby beings unconsciously step back. "Come on, let us enjoy!"
Emotive descended to hover near THE Living Concept, who regarded this arrival with the resignation of someone who knew their evening had just become complicated.
"Do you want to know the purpose of this Festival?" Concept asked, perhaps hoping that understanding might encourage departure.
THE Living Emotive's smile shifted into something that made nearby Sacred Herbs wilt.

"Does it matter what the purpose is? This is a feast and festival to feed." The pause that followed carried weight that made gravity jealous. "And sometimes, you have to fatten the pigs before you lead them to slaughter."
BOOM!
The words landed like a blade wrapped in silk. THE Living Concept's form actually recoiled, ideas within it reconfiguring rapidly as implications cascaded through its consciousness.
The philosophy of fattening pigs for slaughter...such an agricultural metaphor for such a grand gathering!

Make them comfortable. Let them feast. Allow them to believe they're honored guests rather than eventual offerings. The kindness isn't kindness; it's preparation. The generosity isn't generous; it's investment in a future harvest!
Every festival, in this light, becomes suspect.
Every feast carries the question: are we celebrating, or are we being celebrated? Are we guests at the table, or are we eventually the meal?

THE Living Emotive stood at that grand festival, watching Early Creatures feast on impossible delicacies, watching them grow stronger, more complex, more valuable. Watching them fatten on gifts and honors and recognition.
On that day, who knew what THE Living Emotive meant by those words? Who could have predicted that sometimes the most dangerous predator is the one that feeds you first?

The festival continued, of course. The music played, the food was consumed, the ceremonies proceeded. But something had shifted. A shadow had fallen across the celebration, subtle as emotion but persistent as feeling.
Some say that was the last truly grand festival of the Earliest Folds. After that, gatherings became smaller, more cautious.
Trust... became a luxury that even beings of immense power couldn't quite afford.
After all, once you've heard someone compare a feast to fattening pigs for slaughter, it's hard to enjoy the meal without wondering when the butcher arrives!

After all, once you've heard someone compare a feast to fattening pigs for slaughter, it's hard to enjoy the meal without wondering when the butcher arrives!

chapters.title: Chapter 4221 Feasts and Festivals! V
paragraphs: In the current Era.
In the Early Veiled Shore.
The fervor of their unified cry, "Whatever it takes," still lingered in the air of the Radiant Shore, an electrical charge of pure, unadulterated purpose.
The feast continued, but its nature had changed. It was no longer a simple celebration of a single victory, but the solemn, joyous meal of a people who had accepted their shared, desperate destiny.
The taste of the concept-infused fish was still a symphony on the tongue, but now each bite was a reminder of the desperation they had chosen to embrace, the power they had to accumulate!
Malphas, a silent, graceful shadow amidst the radiant light, moved through the gathering.
Noah watched it all calmly.
As he was observing the glorious scene, the figure of Malphas appeared before him, a silent, respectful presence.
He bowed lightly, his crimson eyes holding a deep, analytical light.
"My Lord," he began, his voice a low, cultured baritone that cut through the ambient joy of the feast.
He conjured a shadowy screen in the air before Noah, a window into another time, another place.
"I have a report."
The screen flickered to life, showing the chaotic, war-torn skies of the Transcendent Origin Folds. From this impossible vantage point, Malphas's narration began.
"Schrodinger's movements were... masterful," he said, his tone holding a professional, almost chilling, respect.

"He used the chaos of the battle, the very presence of The Dead, as a cloak. His paradoxical weavings allowed him to move undetected, evading the defensive measures of those still remaining in the Heart of Origin. He bypassed reserve forces that, I can confirm, hold power equal to or even greater than the nine-headed turtle."
HUUM!

The shadowy screen zoomed in, following a faint, almost imperceptible distortion in the fabric of spacetime. "His purpose was twofold," Malphas continued. "One, we do not yet know. He made his weavings murky, even to my perception, for a brief, critical moment within the Heart of Origin. The other purpose, however, is now clear. He went to free a prisoner."
The screen shifted, showing a deep, hidden chamber within the Heart of Origin, a prison carved from the very concept of immutability.
And within it, a woman. She was wrapped in a tattered, obsidian robe, held together by chains that seemed to be forged from solidified paradoxes and origins.
She was on her knees, her form so frail she did not even seem capable of walking. But then she looked up, and her eyes... her eyes held a terrifying, untamed power, a gaze that could unmake Folds!
As if she could feel the gaze of Malphas's crows upon her, she turned and looked directly at the screen.
And in that moment, both she and Schrodinger, who had just appeared beside her, vanished.
"Her name," Malphas said, his voice a low, somber note, "from the little I was able to extract from her weavings... is Leonore Rureaux."
The name echoed in the quiet space around Noah. And then, a sharp gasp.
"Leonore Rureaux?!"
Moiraine shot to her feet, her usual serene, paradoxical grace shattered.
Her eyes were shining with a brilliant, fervent light, a mixture of awe, respect, and a dawning, terrible dread.

"She...was a legend," Moiraine whispered, her voice buzzing. "One of the oldest, most powerful Living Paradoxes, a close, devoted follower of THE Living Paradox themselves. The stories said she was a force of nature, a being whose command of paradox was so absolute she could turn an enemy's own strength into the weapon of their demise!"
WAA!
She took a deep, shuddering breath, what she knew of her people spilling from her.

"Eons ago, she was injured in a battle in the Wandering Territories. The Coalition of Living Existences saw their chance. They ambushed her with their strongest while she was at her weakest. She stood against them all, alone. The battle was said to have shattered three entire Folds. We all believed she had fallen, that she had been collapsed in that final, glorious stand. But... it seems she was alive. They didn't kill her. They kept her locked up, all this time."
Noah listened, his expression a mask of cold, analytical calm.
"So," he said, his voice cutting through the heavy, emotional atmosphere, "what does Schrodinger want with this Leonore Rureaux?"

Moiraine pondered this, her mind racing. "Leonore was more than just powerful. She was a leader, a figure that all Living Paradoxes would follow without question. Schrodinger has attained a similar height, but she... she was above it. Her return... I can't imagine what it would mean."
Malphas looked between his Lord and Moiraine, then bowed. "I will expand my reach into the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds. I will endeavor to obtain more information, My Lord."
Noah gave a single, permissive nod. As Malphas turned to leave, another figure approached, her steps hesitant but her eyes filled with a new, burning determination.
It was Liora.
She bowed respectfully before Noah. "Sir," she began, her voice a soft, yet firm, plea. "I wonder... if it would be okay for me to go and rescue my Father? With the power I have now..."
She fiddled with the fabric of her white dress as she spoke. Noah smiledm
He remembered Bob. Or, as Thauron had liked to call him, Little Bobby!
He looked at Liora, at the young woman who now radiated a power in excess of 10 Trillion, a power that now surpassed her own father's.
He gave her a nod. "Bob is in the lands of The Living Laws, touring a prison while devouring the Paradoxes jailed there. You can go, but..."
As he spoke, a figure walked up from behind Liora. His son, Henry.
"I... will accompany her, Father." he said, his voice steady and confident. "And I'll take a few others, to ensure that everything goes smoothly."
Noah's eyes, sharp and assessing, moved between Henry and Liora. He saw the quiet resolve in his son's eyes, the grateful hope in Liora's.
He smiled calmly, then turned his gaze towards the Inevitability Ranch Sanctuary.
"Take one of these little guys as well," he said.
He beckoned, and one of the young Inevitabilities, the one that had taken a liking to him, came bouncing over like a happy, terrifyingly powerful puppy.
Henry reached out and stroked its writhing tentacles with a calm, familiar gesture. He looked over at Lilith, Ayame, Lodovico, The Bard of Quintessence, and a few others.
A small party was forming, a rescue mission into the heart of the Living Laws' domain. A party of ridiculously powerful Dukes!
Liora gave a light, grateful bow to Noah. He waved his hand, and a radiant, white-gold light enveloped them.
In the next instant, they were gone!

chapters.title: Chapter 4222 Bobby! I
paragraphs: In a Fold under the control of Living Laws...there was the Juridicial Sanctum!
The Juridical Sanctum of the Living Laws was a place of profound, unnerving stillness.
It was a realm carved from a single, unified concept: absolute, unyielding Law.
Pristine floors of white marble, polished to a mirror sheen, stretched out in every direction, reflecting a sky that was not a sky at all, but a luminous, featureless expanse of pure, white light.
From these floors, massive marbled pillars, each one a testament to the unshakeable foundations of Law, rose to meet that impossible sky.
All around, in silent, solemn rows, stood massive statues of white crystal and stone.

They were effigies of famous Dukes of Law from across the eons, each one depicted with a blindfold over their eyes and holding a different type of scale, a silent, eternal testament to the idea that justice was blind and that all things could be weighed.
The air itself was cold, sterile, and utterly silent.
And into this perfect, sterile silence, chaos arrived.
A brilliant, white-gold light flashed into existence...and then they were there.
Henry, Liora, Lilith, Ayame, Lodovico, the Bard of Quintessence, and a single, writhing, and curiously happy Young Inevitability.
They had barely materialized, their auras of Duke-level power a riot of color and energy in this monochrome world, when they realized they were not alone!
Directly ahead of them, a patrol of Honored and Prime Living Laws, their forms shimmering with the silver-white light of their authority, had been moving across the marbled expanse.
They stopped, their mouths agape, their eyes wide with a shock so profound it seemed to have momentarily broken their connection to the very laws of existence they embodied.
Henry smiled wryly. A flicker of his father's own tyrannical amusement danced in his eyes.
He knew his father could have placed them in the deepest, most secure cell, directly in front of Bob. But no.
They had been dropped at what was likely the very entrance to this vast prison, light-years from their target, directly in front of a welcoming committee.
'Is he testing me?' Henry thought. 'Trying to get me to flex my muscles a bit?'
He stepped forward, his movements casual, his smile disarming.
"Hey there," he said, his voice echoing in the vast, silent space. "We're just here to grab one person. You won't give us any trouble, will you?"
The Living Laws were dumbstruck. They could feel it- the crushing, undeniable weight of the beings before them.
Dukes! All of them.
Beings that could flatten them, their laws, and this entire section of the Sanctum in a single, thoughtless instant.
For a long moment, there was only a stunned silence. Then, the leading Honored Living Law, a being whose face was a mask of stern, ancient judgment, did something unexpected.
His expression broke into a wide, almost manic smile.
"Wow!" he exclaimed, his voice filled with a theatrical awe. "We did not see anything at all! In fact, I believe we saw some Sirs who seem to be in need of directions? And perhaps... keys?"
With a flourish, the Honored Living Law took out a set of shimmering, crystalline keys and tossed them towards Henry.
He...was just an Honored Living Law. Was he to just throw his life away? He wanted to live!
He then turned to the other, still-frozen Living Laws, his expression becoming deadly serious.
"Sometimes," he said, his voice a low, profound declaration, "for the sake of greater peace, the Law must be blind."
He then stood ramrod straight, his arms crossed, his eyes closed, a perfect imitation of the statues that surrounded them.
The other Laws, after a moment of stunned hesitation, followed his lead. They became a living, breathing wall of willful ignorance...all for the sake of their lives!
Henry shook his head with a smile. He caught the keys and turned to his party.
"Wait here," he said, his eyes finding Liora's. She was a tempest of conflicting emotions, her gaze a mixture of desperate hope and anxious concern.
He gave her a reassuring nod.
He breathed in, and he felt it. The burgeoning, impossible power that was his birthright.
|You are the only Progeny of The Early Creature, Osmont.|
|Your Existence, born of such a unique and powerful lineage, has begun to retroactively attempt to produce the Blood of an Early Creature.|
|Your heart is unfathomably strong. In the future, you stand a chance of inheriting the Heart of an Early Creature.|
Henry smiled, a true, brilliant expression of pure, unadulterated confidence. It was the power of his father, a legacy that was only just beginning to awaken within him.
|O True Emperor of Nepotism, which abilities of your Father do you wish to utilize?|
He didn't have to think. He sent the command, a silent, arrogant whisper to the very fabric of his being.
'Plot. Put the True Source of Plot to use. Make it so that we stand right before Bob in the next second.'
HUUM!
A blinding, golden light, the very color of narrative destiny, wrapped around him and his companions.
|The Weavings of Plot have been invoked. A long and tedious journey has been deemed... unnecessary for the current narrative.|
|Existence itself is being bent. The scenic route is being skipped.|
|Cutting across the vast prison of the Living Laws... now.|
BOOM!
The marbled floors and pillars of the Sanctum cracked, not from a physical impact, but from the sheer, narrative force of their departure.
In the next moment, their figures materialized light-years away, in the deepest heart of the prison.
They reappeared in a vast, cold void, filled with massive, floating white cages. Most of these cages were torn open, their occupants either escaped or... consumed.
They stood before one cage that was still intact.
Inside, a figure with white-gold skin and a perfectly round, bald head that shone with a brilliant light was licking his lips, as if he had just finished a hearty meal.
Bob!
Little Bobby!

chapters.title: Chapter 4223 Bobby! II
paragraphs: His eyes, wide and filled with a wild, almost feral light, snapped towards them. His jaw dropped. "Liora?"
"Father!" Liora cried, a wave of pure, unrestrained joy washing over her. She rushed forward, phasing through the bars of the cage and throwing her arms around him in a fierce embrace.
But at the same time...
HUUM!
"WHO DARES?!"
A booming shout echoed through the void. The aura of a Duke of Law, a power of at least 30 Trillion, flared from above.
Soon after, hundreds of Honored and Prime Living Laws appeared, their white garbs a stark contrast to the darkness of the void.
The Duke, a woman of cold, breathtaking beauty, was shocked to first sense and then see a group of foreign Dukes in her prison, and she attacked instantly!
White Living Law Authority erupted from her, and above each of Henry's party, a massive white scale, the very symbol of judgment, appeared, seeking to crush them!

Bob paled, his eyes wide with terror. He held his daughter close, his body tensing as a swarm of black tentacles began to surge from his back, ready to reveal his own dark secret to protect her. But before he could...
"It's okay."
Henry's voice was a calm, steady anchor in the storm. He smiled, a perfect echo of his father's own confident, tyrannical grin.
He didn't even move. Bob watched in shock as first, his own daughter, his precious Liora, looked up in anger.
"Who dares interrupt my reunion with my father?!" she roared, and with a single tap of her finger, a torrent of white-gold Origin flames erupted upwards, seeking to melt the very concept of judgment.
At the same time...
Lilith stepped forward.
"Demonic Chains," she purred, and from her, chains of pure, binding Origin authority shot up, intending to shatter the scales.
Ayame followed, a radiant smile on her face. "Sun of Helios," she called, and a miniature white-gold sun, blazing with the heat of a Wheel's core, rose to meet the attack.
Lodovico, the quiet sculptor, took out a simple chisel and struck the air, a conceptual blow that sent cracks racing up the descending scales!
And finally, the Bard of Quintessence, the simian being with fur of white-gold, struck a single, resonant note on his lute. A wave of pure, terrifying melody crashed upwards!
And amidst it all, the Young Inevitability, with a happy, gurgling sound, sent its own writhing tentacles into the fray, eager to devour everything.
The combined assault of these newly-minted Dukes was a symphony of destruction.
The Duke of Law's attack was not just pushed back; it was annihilated.
The massive scales shattered, and the shockwave of their power ripped through the very sky of the Juridical Sanctum, tearing the prison itself in half in this area!
Amidst this shocking display of power, Henry looked at Bob and Liora.
He was about to tell them it was time to go when he heard a familiar voice of his Father in his mind, a calm, commanding whisper from across the Folds.
'Stay for a little while longer. Fight the Dukes that come. Get some experience.'
HUUM!
Henry was astonished. But he listened, and he nodded. He turned to his companions, a wide smile on his face.
"Okay, everyone," he announced, his voice filled with a joyous, battle-hungry light!
"We will stay a little bit longer and have a training exercise."
Bob heard this, and his mind reeled. "What?" he cried, his voice a mixture of incredulity and disbelief. "No, we must leave before-"
Henry turned to him and shook his head calmly. "Father wants us to have this training exercise, so we will have it. After that, we'll go."
A training exercise. He had truly called this a training exercise.
Bob turned to his daughter, expecting to see some semblance of common sense, some urgency to leave.
But... huh? He blinked, looking at her.
She was gazing at Henry, a radiant, smiling, almost adoring look on her face, a look he did not like at all!
He protectively wrapped his arms around his daughter, his own gaze turning cautious as he looked at Henry.
Was someone trying to get their hands on his precious daughter?!
He couldn't affirm things right now, but the Inevitability within him buzzed with a hungry light as he remembered his ailment and pulled back from his daughter slightly.
Right. There was still the ordeal of the Mutated Inevitability inside him he had to deal with to make sure he didn't hurt anyone around him!
In the Folds of the Living Laws, a prison break and training exercise continued.
But in another location, a prison break has already occured as the one who used to be prisoner had been whisked away!
Far from any known locations.
In a veiled weaving of Existence.
Schrodinger and the entity he supported arrived not with a bang, but with the quiet sigh of displaced reality.
One moment, they were in the chaotic, war-torn skies of the Transcendent Origin Folds, and the next, their feet touched the dark, damp sand of a world that had forgotten the sun.
Murky, listless waters sloshed behind them, a sea the color of old bruises.
Ahead, a massive, continental-sized landmass stretched to a horizon that was lost in a perpetual, colorless twilight.
It had the bones of an Early Veiled Shore, the grand, impossible scale of a place forged by primordial power. But it was a skeleton, a memory.
It had none of the vibrant, white-gold brilliance, none of the teeming, vivid life!

Grand, ancient structures, their architecture echoing the abodes of Early Creatures, rose like monuments to a forgotten age, their surfaces worn smooth by eons of a wind that carried no scent of life.

In some regions of the vast continent, plots of farmland had been cleared, and a few, hardy-looking Sacred Herbs were being cultivated, but the very soil seemed harsh, tired, and not conducive to growth.
This was a place of struggle, a sanctuary built on the edge of oblivion!
And yet, it was not empty. The air was thick with the auras of tens of thousands of scattered lifeforms, a shocking, impossible congregation of all ten different types of Living Existences!

HUUM!
"WHO DARES?!"
A booming shout echoed through the void.
The aura of a Duke of Law, a power of at least 30 Trillion, flared from above.
Soon after, hundreds of Honored and Prime Living Laws appeared, their white garbs a stark contrast to the darkness of the void.
The Duke, a woman of cold, breathtaking beauty, was shocked to first sense and then see a group of foreign Dukes in her prison, and she attacked instantly!
White Living Law Authority erupted from her, and above each of Henry's party, a massive white scale, the very symbol of judgment, appeared, seeking to crush them!
Bob paled, his eyes wide with terror.
He held his daughter close, his body tensing as a swarm of black tentacles began to surge from his back, ready to reveal his own dark secret to protect her.
But before he could...
"It's okay."
Henry's voice was a calm, steady anchor in the storm.
He smiled, a perfect echo of his father's own confident, tyrannical grin.
He didn't even move.
Bob watched in shock as first, his own daughter, his precious Liora, looked up in anger.
"Who dares interrupt my reunion with my father?!" she roared, and with a single tap of her finger, a torrent of white-gold Origin flames erupted upwards, seeking to melt the very concept of judgment.
At the same time...
Lilith stepped forward.
"Demonic Chains," she purred, and from her, chains of pure, binding Origin authority shot up, intending to shatter the scales.
Ayame followed, a radiant smile on her face.
"Sun of Helios," she called, and a miniature white-gold sun, blazing with the heat of a Wheel's core, rose to meet the attack.
Lodovico, the quiet sculptor, took out a simple chisel and struck the air, a conceptual blow that sent cracks racing up the descending scales!
And finally, the Bard of Quintessence, the simian being with fur of white-gold, struck a single, resonant note on his lute.
A wave of pure, terrifying melody crashed upwards!
And amidst it all, the Young Inevitability, with a happy, gurgling sound, sent its own writhing tentacles into the fray, eager to devour everything.
The combined assault of these newly-minted Dukes was a symphony of destruction.
The Duke of Law's attack was not just pushed back; it was annihilated.
The massive scales shattered, and the shockwave of their power ripped through the very sky of the Juridical Sanctum, tearing the prison itself in half in this area!
Amidst this shocking display of power, Henry looked at Bob and Liora.
He was about to tell them it was time to go when he heard a familiar voice of his Father in his mind, a calm, commanding whisper from across the Folds.
'Stay for a little while longer.
Fight the Dukes that come.
Get some experience.'
HUUM!
Henry was astonished.
But he listened, and he nodded.
He turned to his companions, a wide smile on his face.
"Okay, everyone," he announced, his voice filled with a joyous, battle-hungry light!
"We will stay a little bit longer and have a training exercise."
Bob heard this, and his mind reeled.
"What?" he cried, his voice a mixture of incredulity and disbelief.
"No, we must leave before-"
Henry turned to him and shook his head calmly.
"Father wants us to have this training exercise, so we will have it.
After that, we'll go."
A training exercise.
He had truly called this a training exercise.
Bob turned to his daughter, expecting to see some semblance of common sense, some urgency to leave.
But... huh?
He blinked, looking at her.
She was gazing at Henry, a radiant, smiling, almost adoring look on her face, a look he did not like at all!
He protectively wrapped his arms around his daughter, his own gaze turning cautious as he looked at Henry.
Was someone trying to get their hands on his precious daughter?!
He couldn't affirm things right now, but the Inevitability within him buzzed with a hungry light as he remembered his ailment and pulled back from his daughter slightly.
Right.
There was still the ordeal of the Mutated Inevitability inside him he had to deal with to make sure he didn't hurt anyone around him!
In the Folds of the Living Laws, a prison break and training exercise continued.
But in another location, a prison break has already occured as the one who used to be prisoner had been whisked away!
Far from any known locations.
In a veiled weaving of Existence.
Schrodinger and the entity he supported arrived not with a bang, but with the quiet sigh of displaced reality.
One moment, they were in the chaotic, war-torn skies of the Transcendent Origin Folds, and the next, their feet touched the dark, damp sand of a world that had forgotten the sun.
Murky, listless waters sloshed behind them, a sea the color of old bruises.
Ahead, a massive, continental-sized landmass stretched to a horizon that was lost in a perpetual, colorless twilight.
It had the bones of an Early Veiled Shore, the grand, impossible scale of a place forged by primordial power.
But it was a skeleton, a memory.
It had none of the vibrant, white-gold brilliance, none of the teeming, vivid life!

Grand, ancient structures, their architecture echoing the abodes of Early Creatures, rose like monuments to a forgotten age, their surfaces worn smooth by eons of a wind that carried no scent of life.

In some regions of the vast continent, plots of farmland had been cleared, and a few, hardy-looking Sacred Herbs were being cultivated, but the very soil seemed harsh, tired, and not conducive to growth.
This was a place of struggle, a sanctuary built on the edge of oblivion!
And yet, it was not empty.
The air was thick with the auras of tens of thousands of scattered lifeforms, a shocking, impossible congregation of all ten different types of Living Existences!

chapters.title: Chapter 4224 Dessicated!
paragraphs: As Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux touched down, a figure emerged from a nearby, half-tended field.
It was Duke Valen, the blind Duke of Origin, his wizened, bearded face etched with a deep, abiding concern.
He moved forward to help Schrodinger, who was supporting the frail, trembling form of Leonore. Behind him, other figures paused in their work.
Dukes of Living Temporals, their forms flickering in and out of the present. Living Elementals, who seemed to be trying to coax warmth back into the dead soil.
Even other Living Paradoxes, their expressions a mixture of surprise and wary respect.
Schrodinger waved a hand, a gentle, dismissive gesture. "It is okay," he said, his voice carrying a quiet authority that sought no argument.
"I will tend to her without an issue."
Duke Valen and the others nodded, their gazes lingering on the woman Schrodinger supported.
Her right arm was wrapped around his shoulders, her form so weak and feeble it seemed a strong breeze could unmake her.
And yet, the Dukes were astonished to see that between these two beings of Paradox, no Inevitabilities formed!
The air remained stable, calm. It was a violation of a fundamental law, a paradox within a paradox. Why was that?
Their curiosity piqued, Duke Valen and a few others allowed their own authorities to gently reach out, to try and perceive a little more of this new entrant.
But the moment their senses brushed against her, her head lifted. Her crimson eyes, which had been half-closed in exhaustion, opened fully and glanced at them.

It was a look devoid of malice, of anger, of anything at all. And yet, in that empty gaze, they felt a weight so profound, so absolutely terrifying, that they all trembled and instinctively averted their own senses, a cold, primal dread flooding their beings!
Schrodinger led Leonore across the Desiccated Sleeping Shore, his movements filled with a tenderness that was a stark contrast to his usual, chaotic nature.
His arm was a firm, steady support around her waist, his pace measured to match her faltering steps.
Everywhere they passed, whether by the struggling farmlands or the grand, silent structures, the powerful beings of this hidden sanctuary would pause and offer a nod of profound respect.
Dukes who could have commanded Folds, Royals whose very presence was a law, all acknowledged Schrodinger not as a peer, but as a leader!
They eventually arrived at an Abode that stood before a clear, blue pond, a single point of vibrant life in this otherwise desolate landscape.
Schrodinger waved his hand, and a paradoxical golden film of light, both transparent and opaque, covered the entire area, isolating them from all outside perception.

He tenderly set Leonore down at the edge of the pond, her legs submerged in the cool, clear water. The moment her skin touched the water, it began to shine with a unique, healing energy that flowed into her body.
For a long moment, there was silence. Then, Leonore spoke, her voice a dry, cracked whisper.
"Any luck?"

Schrodinger shook his head, a gesture of profound, weary disappointment. He waved his hands, and a collection of terrifyingly complex herbs and items...a crystallized tear of a weeping Wheel, the powdered heart of a concept that had died of loneliness, and more materialized and floated towards Leonore, fusing into her body and bringing a faint, vibrant glow back to her pale complexion.

"In all these years, not much progress has been made," he said, his voice heavy. "More forces were gathered here, as you saw. But THE Loom... it remains impenetrable. It was designed that way... as you told me yourself."
HUUM!
An immense, suffocating silence descended.
Leonore said nothing, her gaze lost in the shimmering waters of the pond. Eventually, Schrodinger finished his work and came to sit beside her.
Her eyes, which had been vacant, began to blaze with a defiant, burning light.

"At this point," she said, her voice a low, venomous hiss, "I just want to prove them wrong. Even if they deemed me defective, not up to par to enter with those permitted entry into THE Loom. Even if the one I looked up to the most left me behind... I just want to do it to spite them. To show them that they were wrong."
She paused, the fire in her eyes dimming slightly, replaced by a deep, aching vulnerability.
"But... it is hard."
The words were a quiet confession of a pain that had festered for eons. Schrodinger looked ahead, his gaze calm, yet filled with a confidence that seemed to defy the very reality of their situation.
"We will find a way," he said, his voice a steady, unwavering promise. "Before the clock runs out, we will find a way. You will not experience any collapse or Fallout. This, I promise you."
At his words, Leonore smiled, a sad, beautiful, and utterly heartbreaking expression.
She shook her head, and as she did, her body began to brim with a terrifying purity, a power that easily reached into the dozens of Quadrillions!
"There you go again," she whispered, "making promises you cannot fulfill."
After her words, a comfortable silence settled between them. They simply sat, their feet in the glowing water, two ancient beings against an impossible doom.
It was Leonore who spoke up first, her voice a little stronger now. "What is next?"
Schrodinger's gaze sharpened, his mind, ever the strategist, turning to the new variables on the board.

"First, we have to get you acclimated to a few changes. Some new players. There are the forces from the Sanctuary of The First Farmer, who may have something. And there is also this... Osmont. Someone that is likely an Early Creature, or maybe not."
"Oh?" Leonore blinked, a flicker of genuine interest in her crimson eyes.
Schrodinger smiled and nodded. "There are many possibilities," he said, his voice a low, thoughtful hum. "We simply need to see which ones will help us find the solution to survive what is coming."
